وَقَالَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً وَاحِدَةً ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤَادَكَ ۖ وَرَتَّلْنَاهُ تَرْتِيلًا [25:32]
Those who reject Faith say: "Why is not the Qur´an revealed to him all at once? Thus (is it revealed), that We may strengthen thy heart thereby, and We have rehearsed it to thee in slow, well-arranged stages, gradually. [25:32]
b: And those who disbelieve say, ‘Why has the Qur’ān not been revealed to him all at once?’, as the Torah, the Gospel and the Book of Psalms [were]. God, exalted be He, says: We have revealed it, thus, in parts, [it is], that We may strengthen your inner-heart with it, and We have arranged it in a specific order, that is to say, We produce it in stages one part after another, gradually and deliberately, in order to facilitate its comprehension and its memorisation.

f:
وَلَا يَأْتُونَكَ بِمَثَلٍ إِلَّا جِئْنَاكَ بِالْحَقِّ وَأَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا [25:33]
And no question do they bring to thee but We reveal to thee the truth and the best explanation (thereof). [25:33]
b: And they do not bring you any similitude, to invalidate your mission, but that We bring you the truth, that refutes it, and [what is] better [as] exposition, explanation.

f:
الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلَىٰ جَهَنَّمَ أُولَٰئِكَ شَرٌّ مَكَانًا وَأَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا [25:34]
Those who will be gathered to Hell (prone) on their faces,- they will be in an evil plight, and, as to Path, most astray. [25:34]
b: They are, those who will be gathered on their faces, that is, [those who] will be driven [as cattle], toward Hell: they will be in the worst place, namely, Hell, and furthest astray from the way, [they will be] on a path of error worse than that of others; and this [path] is their disbelief.

f:
وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ وَجَعَلْنَا مَعَهُ أَخَاهُ هَارُونَ وَزِيرًا [25:35]
(Before this,) We sent Moses عليه السلام The Book, and appointed his brother Aaron with him as minister; [25:35]
b: And verily We gave Moses عليه السلام the Scripture, the Torah, and made Aaron, his brother, [go] with him as a minister, an assistant.

f:
فَقُلْنَا اذْهَبَا إِلَى الْقَوْمِ الَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَدَمَّرْنَاهُمْ تَدْمِيرًا [25:36]
And We command: "Go ye both, to the people who have rejected our Signs:" And those (people) We destroyed with utter destruction. [25:36]
b: Then We said, ‘Go both of you to the people who have denied Our signs’, that is, to the Egyptians — Pharaoh and his folk. So they went to them with the Message but they [the Egyptians] denied both of them. Then We destroyed them utterly.

f:
وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ لَمَّا كَذَّبُوا الرُّسُلَ أَغْرَقْنَاهُمْ وَجَعَلْنَاهُمْ لِلنَّاسِ آيَةً ۖ وَأَعْتَدْنَا لِلظَّالِمِينَ عَذَابًا أَلِيمًا [25:37]
And the people of Noah عليه السلام,- when they rejected the messengers, We drowned them, and We made them as a Sign for mankind; and We have prepared for (all) wrong-doers a grievous Penalty;- [25:37]
b: And, mention, the people of Noah عليه السلام, when they denied the messengers, in denying Noah عليه السلام — it is as though he were many messengers given the length of time he remained among them; or [it is thus expressed in the plural] because to deny him is [equivalent] to denying all the other messengers, for they all came with the same [Message concerning] affirmation of God’s Oneness — We drowned them (this is the response to lammā, ‘when’) and made them a sign, a lesson, for mankind, thereafter, and We have prepared, in the Hereafter, for the evildoers, the disbelievers, a painful chastisement, in addition to what [chastisement] may befall them in this world.

f:
وَعَادًا وَثَمُودَ وَأَصْحَابَ الرَّسِّ وَقُرُونًا بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ كَثِيرًا [25:38]
As also ´Ad and Thamud, and the Companions of the Rass, and many a generation between them. [25:38]
b: And, mention, ‘Ād, the people of Hūd, and Thamūd, the people of Sālih, and the dwellers at al-Rass (al-rass) — the name of a ‘well’; their prophet is said to have been Shu‘ayb; although some say it was someone else. [The story is that] they had been sitting around it [on one occasion] when it collapsed beneath them [burying them] together with their dwellings. And many generations, peoples, in between, that is, between [the people of] ‘Ād and the dwellers at al-Rass.

f:
وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنَا لَهُ الْأَمْثَالَ ۖ وَكُلًّا تَبَّرْنَا تَتْبِيرًا [25:39]
To each one We set forth Parables and examples; and each one We broke to utter annihilation (for their sins). [25:39]
b: For each [of them] We struck similitudes, when establishing arguments against them, and We destroyed them only after warning [them], and each [of them] We ruined utterly, We destroyed utterly, because of their denial of the prophets sent to them.

f:
وَلَقَدْ أَتَوْا عَلَى الْقَرْيَةِ الَّتِي أُمْطِرَتْ مَطَرَ السَّوْءِ ۚ أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَهَا ۚ بَلْ كَانُوا لَا يَرْجُونَ نُشُورًا [25:40]
And the (Unbelievers) must indeed have passed by the town on which was rained a shower of evil: did they not then see it (with their own eyes)? But they fear not the Resurrection. [25:40]
b: And verily they, namely, the disbelievers of Mecca, will have passed by the town on which an evil shower was rained (al-saw’, ‘evil’, is the verbal noun from sā’a, ‘was evil’), that is, [it was showered] with stones. This was the principal town of the towns inhabited by the people of Lot; God destroyed its inhabitants for their committing acts of lewdness. Can it be that they have not seen it?, on their journeys to Syria, and so take heed thereof? (the interrogative is affirmative). Nay, but it is that they do not expect, they have [no] fear of [any], resurrection, and so they do not believe.

f:
وَإِذَا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُوًا أَهَٰذَا الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا [25:41]
When they see thee, they treat thee no otherwise than in mockery: "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?" [25:41]
b: And when they see you, they take you in mockery only, as an object of derision, saying, ‘Is this the one whom God has sent as a messenger?, as he is wont to claim? — contemptuously of him as one not worthy of being a messenger.

f:
إِنْ كَادَ لَيُضِلُّنَا عَنْ آلِهَتِنَا لَوْلَا أَنْ صَبَرْنَا عَلَيْهَا ۚ وَسَوْفَ يَعْلَمُونَ حِينَ يَرَوْنَ الْعَذَابَ مَنْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا [25:42]
"He indeed would well-nigh have misled us from our gods, had it not been that we were constant to them!" - Soon will they know, when they see the Penalty, who it is that is most misled in Path! [25:42]
b: Indeed (in, softened in place of the hardened form, with its subject omitted, namely, innahu) he was about to lead us astray, turn us away, from our gods, had we not stood by them’, he would have turned us away from them. God, exalted be He, says: And soon they will know, when they behold the chastisement, with their own eyes in the Hereafter, who is further astray from the way, who is further upon the path of error: they or the believers?

f:
أَرَأَيْتَ مَنِ اتَّخَذَ إِلَٰهَهُ هَوَاهُ أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا [25:43]
Seest thou such a one as taketh for his god his own passion (or impulse)? Couldst thou be a disposer of affairs for him? [25:43]
b: Have you seen — inform Me [about] — him who has taken as his god his own desire?, that is, as something that will be bring about his ruin (the indirect object [ilāhahu, ‘as his god’] precedes the direct object because it is more important; the clause [beginning] man ittakhadha, ‘him who has taken’, constitutes the first direct object of a-ra’ayta, ‘have you seen’, the second being [the following, a-fa-anta …]) Will you be a guardian over him?, a protector to preserve him from following his desires? No.

f:
أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ ۚ إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعَامِ ۖ بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا [25:44]
Or thinkest thou that most of them listen or understand? They are only like cattle;- nay, they are worse astray in Path. [25:44]
b: Or do you suppose that most of them listen, listening so as to understand, or comprehend?, what you say to them? They are but as the cattle — nay, but they are further astray from the way, further from these [cattle] upon the path of misguidance, for at least they [cattle] yield to the person who looks after them, whereas these [disbelievers] do not obey their Master, Who is gracious to them.

f:
أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ كَيْفَ مَدَّ الظِّلَّ وَلَوْ شَاءَ لَجَعَلَهُ سَاكِنًا ثُمَّ جَعَلْنَا الشَّمْسَ عَلَيْهِ دَلِيلًا [25:45]
Hast thou not turned thy vision to thy Lord?- How He doth prolong the shadow! If He willed, He could make it stationary! then do We make the sun its guide; [25:45]
b: Have you not seen, contemplated, the work of, your Lord, how He extends the [twilight] shadow?, from the point of daybreak to the point of sunrise. For had He, your Lord, willed, He would have made it still, ever-present so that it does not disappear with the rising of the sun. Then We made the sun an indicator of it, [of] the shadow; were it not for the sun the shadow would not have been known.

f:
ثُمَّ قَبَضْنَاهُ إِلَيْنَا قَبْضًا يَسِيرًا [25:46]
Then We draw it in towards Ourselves,- a contraction by easy stages. [25:46]
b: Then We retract it, the extended shadow, to Us by gentle retraction, subtle [retraction], through the rising of the sun.

f:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِبَاسًا وَالنَّوْمَ سُبَاتًا وَجَعَلَ النَّهَارَ نُشُورًا [25:47]
And He it is Who makes the Night as a Robe for you, and Sleep as Repose, and makes the Day (as it were) a Resurrection. [25:47]
b: And He it is Who made for you the night as a garment, veiling [you] like a garment, and sleep for repose, rest for bodies through the [temporary] cessation of labour, and He made the day for rising, [a time] in which all rise to seek their livelihood and so on.

f:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ الرِّيَاحَ بُشْرًا بَيْنَ يَدَيْ رَحْمَتِهِ ۚ وَأَنْزَلْنَا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً طَهُورًا [25:48]
And He it is Who sends the winds as heralds of glad tidings, going before His mercy, and We send down pure water from the sky,- [25:48]
b: And He it is Who sends forth the winds (al-riyāha; a variant has al-rīha, ‘the wind’) dispersing before His mercy (nushuran, ‘dispersing’), scattered before the [coming of the] rain (a variant reading has nushran, the singular of which is nashūr, similar [in pattern] to rasūl, ‘messenger’ [plural rusul]; another reading has nashran, as a verbal noun; and a third variant has bushran, in other words, [the winds function as] mubashshirāt, ‘bearers of good tidings’, the singular of which is bashīr); and We send down from the heaven purifying water,

f:
لِنُحْيِيَ بِهِ بَلْدَةً مَيْتًا وَنُسْقِيَهُ مِمَّا خَلَقْنَا أَنْعَامًا وَأَنَاسِيَّ كَثِيرًا [25:49]
That with it We may give life to a dead land, and slake the thirst of things We have created,- cattle and men in great numbers. [25:49]
b: with which We revive a dead land (read maytan, in the softened form, equally valid for the masculine and the feminine, but in the masculine [here] because of the [masculine] noun indicating ‘place’ [implicit therein]) and We give it, the water, as drink to the many cattle, camels, cows and sheep, and humans We have created (anāsiyy is the plural of insān: properly it [the plural] should be anāsīn but the [final] nūn has been replaced with a yā’, with which the [other] yā’ has been assimilated; or it [anāsiyy] is [simply] the plural of insiyy).

f:
وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْنَاهُ بَيْنَهُمْ لِيَذَّكَّرُوا فَأَبَىٰ أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُورًا [25:50]
And We have distributed the (water) amongst them, in order that they may celebrate (our) praises, but most men are averse (to aught) but (rank) ingratitude. [25:50]
b: And verily We have distributed it, the water, among them, so that they may remember (li-yadhdhakkarū should actually be li-yatadhakkarū, but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dhāl; a variant reading has li-yadhkurū), that is to say, [so that they may remember] therewith the grace of God. But most people are only intent on ingratitude, on denial of the grace, saying, ‘We have received [this] rain because of such-and-such a storm’.

f:
وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَبَعَثْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ نَذِيرًا [25:51]
Had it been Our Will, We could have sent a warner to every centre of population. [25:51]
b: And had We willed, We could have sent forth in every town a warner, to threaten its inhabitants [with God’s chastisement]; instead We have sent you to the inhabitants of all towns as a warner for your reward to be a great one.

f:
فَلَا تُطِعِ الْكَافِرِينَ وَجَاهِدْهُمْ بِهِ جِهَادًا كَبِيرًا [25:52]
Therefore listen not to the Unbelievers, but strive against them with the utmost strenuousness, with the (Qur´an). [25:52]
b: So do not obey the disbelievers, in their desires, but struggle against them therewith, that is, through [adherence to] the Qur’ān, with a great endeavour.

f:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي مَرَجَ الْبَحْرَيْنِ هَٰذَا عَذْبٌ فُرَاتٌ وَهَٰذَا مِلْحٌ أُجَاجٌ وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَهُمَا بَرْزَخًا وَحِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا [25:53]
It is He Who has let free the two bodies of flowing water: One palatable and sweet, and the other salt and bitter; yet has He made a barrier between them, a partition that is forbidden to be passed. [25:53]
b: And He it is Who merged the two seas: letting them [flow] one adjacent to the other: this one palatable, sweet, and the other saltish, bitter; and He set between the two an isthmus, so that the one does not mix with the other, and a forbidding ban, a shield that prevents the two from becoming mixed.

f:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْمَاءِ بَشَرًا فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَبًا وَصِهْرًا ۗ وَكَانَ رَبُّكَ قَدِيرًا [25:54]
It is He Who has created man from water: then has He established relationships of lineage and marriage: for thy Lord has power (over all things). [25:54]
b: And He it is Who created man from water, [He created] from a sperm-drop a human being, and made for him ties of blood and ties of marriage, whether it be a male or a female, they marry for the purposes of procreation. For your Lord is ever Powerful, with the power to do whatever He will.

f:
وَيَعْبُدُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ مَا لَا يَنْفَعُهُمْ وَلَا يَضُرُّهُمْ ۗ وَكَانَ الْكَافِرُ عَلَىٰ رَبِّهِ ظَهِيرًا [25:55]
Yet do they worship, besides Allah, things that can neither profit them nor harm them: and the Misbeliever is a helper (of Evil), against his own Lord! [25:55]
b: And they, the disbelievers, worship besides God that which neither benefits them, when they worship it, nor harms them, should they refrain therefrom — and these are idols; and the disbeliever is ever a partisan against his Lord, an assistant to Satan through his obedience to him.

f:
وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَاكَ إِلَّا مُبَشِّرًا وَنَذِيرًا [25:56]
But thee We only sent to give glad tidings and admonition. [25:56]
b: And We have not sent you except as a bearer of good tidings, of Paradise, and as a warner, a threatener [of people] with the [chastisement of the] Fire.

f:
قُلْ مَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ إِلَّا مَنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا [25:57]
Say: "No reward do I ask of you for it but this: that each one who will may take a (straight) Path to his Lord." [25:57]
b: Say: ‘I do not ask of you in return for this, that is, for delivering that [Message] with which I have been sent, any reward, except that whoever wishes to follow a way to his Lord [should do so]’, by expending his wealth for the sake of [attaining] God’s pleasure, exalted be He; then [whoever wishes to do so] I will not prevent him from doing so.

f:
وَتَوَكَّلْ عَلَى الْحَيِّ الَّذِي لَا يَمُوتُ وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِهِ ۚ وَكَفَىٰ بِهِ بِذُنُوبِ عِبَادِهِ خَبِيرًا [25:58]
And put thy trust in Him Who lives and dies not; and celebrate his praise; and enough is He to be acquainted with the faults of His servants;- [25:58]
b: And put your trust in the Living One Who does not die, and make glorifications, ensconced, in His praise, in other words, say: subhāna’Llāhi wa’l-hamdu li’Llāh, ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God’. And He suffices as One Aware, as Knower, of the sins of His servants (khabīran, ‘One Aware’, is semantically connected to bi-dhunūbi, ‘of the sins’).

f:
الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامٍ ثُمَّ اسْتَوَىٰ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ ۚ الرَّحْمَٰنُ فَاسْأَلْ بِهِ خَبِيرًا [25:59]
He Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between, in six days, and is firmly established on the Throne (of Authority): Allah Most Gracious: ask thou, then, about Him of any acquainted (with such things). [25:59]
b: He it is, Who created the heavens and the earth and all that is between them in six days, of the [length of the] days of this world, since there was no sun at that point — had He willed He could have created them in an instant, but His not having done so is because He will to teach His creatures to be circumspect — then presided upon the Throne (al-‘arsh in the [classical] language is the seat on which a king sits) the Compassionate One (al-rahmānu substitutes for the subject of [the verb] istawā, ‘presided’) a presiding befitting of Him; so ask, O man, about Him, about the Compassionate One, anyone who is well aware, to inform you about His attributes!

f:
وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ اسْجُدُوا لِلرَّحْمَٰنِ قَالُوا وَمَا الرَّحْمَٰنُ أَنَسْجُدُ لِمَا تَأْمُرُنَا وَزَادَهُمْ نُفُورًا ۩ [25:60]
When it is said to them, "Prostrate to (Allah) Most Gracious!", they say, "And what is (Allah) Most Gracious? Shall we prostrate to that which thou commandest us?" And it increases their flight (from the Truth). [25:60]
b: And when it is said to them, to the disbelievers of Mecca, ‘Prostrate yourselves before the Compassionate One’, they say, ‘And what is the Compassionate One? Should we prostrate ourselves to whatever you bid us’ (ta’murunā; or read ya’murunā, ‘[whatever] he bids us’) — [in both cases] the one bidding is Muhammad (s) — when we do not know who He is? No! And it, this that is said to them, increases their aversion, to faith.

f:
تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ فِي السَّمَاءِ بُرُوجًا وَجَعَلَ فِيهَا سِرَاجًا وَقَمَرًا مُنِيرًا [25:61]
Blessed is He Who made constellations in the skies, and placed therein a Lamp and a Moon giving light; [25:61]
b: God, exalted be He, says: Blessed, magnified, is He Who has placed in the heaven constellations, twelve [of them]: Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo (al-sunbula), Libra, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces. They are the mansions for the seven orbiting planets: Mars rules Aries and Scorpio, Venus: Taurus and Libra, Mercury: Gemini and Virgo, the Moon: Cancer, the Sun: Leo, Jupiter: Sagittarius and Pisces, and Saturn: Capricorn and Aquarius; and has, also, placed in it a lamp, namely, the sun, and a shining moon (a variant reading [for sirājan, ‘sun’] has the plural surujan, which would mean ‘luminous stars’). The moon is singled out for mention because of its particular merit.

f:
وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهَارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَنْ أَرَادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ أَوْ أَرَادَ شُكُورًا [25:62]
And it is He Who made the Night and the Day to follow each other: for such as have the will to celebrate His praises or to show their gratitude. [25:62]
b: And He it is Who made the night and day [to appear] in succession, that is, one succeeding the other, for him who desires to remember (read yadhdhakkara or yadhkura, as before [Q. 25:50]) — so that if he misses [the opportunity to do] some good during the one, he can do it during the other; or desires to be thankful, for the graces of his Lord to him during both [of these periods].

f:
وَعِبَادُ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْنًا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا [25:63]
And the servants of (Allah) Most Gracious are those who walk on the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace!"; [25:63]
b: And the [true] servants of the Compassionate One (‘ibādu’l-rahmāni is the subject, and what comes after it, all the way up to ūlā’ika yujzawna, ‘they will be rewarded’ [of verse 75 below] are adjectival qualifiers of this [subject], with the exception of the parenthetical statements) are those who walk upon the earth modestly, that is, peacefully and humbly, and who, when the ignorant address them, with what they are averse to, say [words of] peace (salām), in other words, words by which they are safe (yaslamūna) from [committing] any sin;

f:
وَالَّذِينَ يَبِيتُونَ لِرَبِّهِمْ سُجَّدًا وَقِيَامًا [25:64]
Those who spend the night in adoration of their Lord prostrate and standing; [25:64]
b: and who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating (sujjad is the plural of sājid) and standing [in worship], in other words, they spend the night performing prayers;

f:
وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا اصْرِفْ عَنَّا عَذَابَ جَهَنَّمَ ۖ إِنَّ عَذَابَهَا كَانَ غَرَامًا [25:65]
Those who say, "Our Lord! avert from us the Wrath of Hell, for its Wrath is indeed an affliction grievous,- [25:65]
b: and who say, ‘Our Lord, avert from us from the chastisement of Hell. Truly its chastisement is abiding, that is, irrevocable.

f:
إِنَّهَا سَاءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا [25:66]
"Evil indeed is it as an abode, and as a place to rest in"; [25:66]
b: It is truly a wretched abode and residence!’, in other words, [it is truly wretched] as a place in which to abide and reside.

f:
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكَانَ بَيْنَ ذَٰلِكَ قَوَامًا [25:67]
Those who, when they spend, are not extravagant and not niggardly, but hold a just (balance) between those (extremes); [25:67]
b: And who, when they expend, upon their dependants, are neither prodigal nor parsimonious (read yaqturū or yuqtirū); but between such, prodigality and parsimony, lies — [between the two] their expenditure [is in] — moderation;

f:
وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَدْعُونَ مَعَ اللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا آخَرَ وَلَا يَقْتُلُونَ النَّفْسَ الَّتِي حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ إِلَّا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا يَزْنُونَ ۚ وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَامًا [25:68]
Those who invoke not, with Allah, any other god, nor slay such life as Allah has made sacred except for just cause, nor commit fornication; - and any that does this (not only) meets punishment. [25:68]
b: and [those] who do not call on another god along with God, nor slay the soul which God has forbidden, that it be slain, except with due cause, and who do not commit fornication — for whoever does that, namely, [whoever does] one of these three things, shall meet with retribution;

f:
يُضَاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذَابُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا [25:69]
(But) the Penalty on the Day of Judgment will be doubled to him, and he will dwell therein in ignominy,- [25:69]
b: doubled (yudā‘af: a variant reading has yuda‘‘af) will be the chastisement for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will abide therein (both verbs may be read in [the imperfect] apocopated form [yudā‘af, ‘it will be doubled’, and yakhlud, ‘he will abide’] as substitutions, or with the [indicative] damma inflection [yudā‘afu and yakhludu] to indicate the beginning of a new sentence) abased (muhānan is a circumstantial qualifier);

f:
إِلَّا مَنْ تَابَ وَآمَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلًا صَالِحًا فَأُولَٰئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ ۗ وَكَانَ اللَّهُ غَفُورًا رَحِيمًا [25:70]
Unless he repents, believes, and works righteous deeds, for Allah will change the evil of such persons into good, and Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful, [25:70]
b: except for him who repents, and believes, and acts righteously, from among them, for such, God will replace their, mentioned, evil deeds with good deeds, in the Hereafter, for God is ever Forgiving, Merciful, that is, He is ever possessed of such attributes;

f:
وَمَنْ تَابَ وَعَمِلَ صَالِحًا فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَابًا [25:71]
And whoever repents and does good has truly turned to Allah with an (acceptable) conversion;- [25:71]
b: and whoever repents, of his sins, from among other than those mentioned, and acts righteously, indeed turns to God with due repentance, that is, he returns to God a sincere return, and God will requite him with good;

f:
وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَشْهَدُونَ الزُّورَ وَإِذَا مَرُّوا بِاللَّغْوِ مَرُّوا كِرَامًا [25:72]
Those who witness no falsehood, and, if they pass by futility, they pass by it with honourable (avoidance); [25:72]
b: and those who do not give false testimony, that is, [testimony containing] mendacity and falsehood, and, when they come across senseless talk, in the way of vile speech and otherwise, they pass by with dignity, shunning such [vanity];

f:
وَالَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِّرُوا بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ لَمْ يَخِرُّوا عَلَيْهَا صُمًّا وَعُمْيَانًا [25:73]
Those who, when they are admonished with the Signs of their Lord, droop not down at them as if they were deaf or blind; [25:73]
b: and those who, when they are reminded, [when] they are admonished, of the revelations of their Lord, that is, [reminded] of the Qur’ān, do not fall on them deaf and blind, but fall [on them] listening, contemplating, benefiting and obedient;

f:
وَالَّذِينَ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا هَبْ لَنَا مِنْ أَزْوَاجِنَا وَذُرِّيَّاتِنَا قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ وَاجْعَلْنَا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِمَامًا [25:74]
And those who pray, "Our Lord! Grant unto us wives and offspring who will be the comfort of our eyes, and give us (the grace) to lead the righteous." [25:74]
b: and those who say, ‘Our Lord! Grant us in our spouses and our offspring (read plural dhurriyyātinā or singular dhurriyyatinā) a joyful sight, for us, so that we see them obedient to You, and make us paragons, of virtue, for the God-fearing’.

f:
أُولَٰئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ بِمَا صَبَرُوا وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيهَا تَحِيَّةً وَسَلَامًا [25:75]
Those are the ones who will be rewarded with the highest place in heaven, because of their patient constancy: therein shall they be met with salutations and peace, [25:75]
b: Those, they will be rewarded with the sublime abode, the highest degree in Paradise, forasmuch as they were steadfast, in obedience to God, and they will be met (read yulaqqawna or yalqawna) therein, in this sublime abode, with a greeting and [words of] peace, from the angels;

f:
خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا [25:76]
Dwelling therein;- how beautiful an abode and place of rest! [25:76]
b: abiding therein. Excellent is it as an abode and station, as a place of residence for them (ūlā’ika, ‘those, they …’, and what comes after it constitute the predicate to the subject ‘ibādu’l-rahmāni, ‘the servants of the Compassionate One’).

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ طسم [26:1]
Ta. Sin. Mim. [26:1]
b: Tā sīn mīm: God knows best what He means by these [letters].

f:
تِلْكَ آيَاتُ الْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ [26:2]
These are verses of the Book that makes (things) clear. [26:2]
b: Those, namely, these signs, are the signs of the Manifest Book, the Qur’ān (the genitive annexation [āyātu’l-kitābi] conveys the [partitive] meaning of min), [the Manifest meaning] the one that manifests what is truth from what is falsehood.

f:
لَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَفْسَكَ أَلَّا يَكُونُوا مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:3]
It may be thou frettest thy soul with grief, that they do not become Believers. [26:3]
b: Perhaps, O Muhammad (s), you might kill yourself, out of distress for the reason, that they, namely, the people of Mecca, will not become believers (la‘alla here expresses sympathy, in other words [what is meant is] ‘have pity on it [your self] by alleviating [the burden of] this distress’).

f:
إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ [26:4]
If (such) were Our Will, We could send down to them from the sky a Sign, to which they would bend their necks in humility. [26:4]
b: If We will We will send down to them a sign from the heaven before which their necks will remain (fa-zallat, [although grammatically in the past tense] is being used in the sense of the imperfect tense) bowed in humility, and they will believe (since ‘necks’ are described as ‘bowed in humility’, [a status] which in fact refers to those who possess them, the adjectival form [khādi‘ūn, ‘bowed in humility’] used therein is the one [normally] used for rational beings).

f:
وَمَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ ذِكْرٍ مِنَ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مُحْدَثٍ إِلَّا كَانُوا عَنْهُ مُعْرِضِينَ [26:5]
But there comes not to them a newly-revealed Message from (Allah) Most Gracious, but they turn away therefrom. [26:5]
b: And there would never come to them from the Compassionate One any remembrance, any [revelation from the] Qur’ān, that is new (muhdathin, is an explicative adjective) but that they used to disregard it.

f:
فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوا فَسَيَأْتِيهِمْ أَنْبَاءُ مَا كَانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ [26:6]
They have indeed rejected (the Message): so they will know soon (enough) the truth of what they mocked at! [26:6]
b: Verily then they have denied, it; but soon there will come to them the news, the consequences, of that which they used to deride.

f:
أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْا إِلَى الْأَرْضِ كَمْ أَنْبَتْنَا فِيهَا مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ كَرِيمٍ [26:7]
Do they not look at the earth,- how many noble things of all kinds We have produced therein? [26:7]
b: Have they not contemplated, observed, the earth, how many We have caused to grow therein, in other words, [We have caused to grow therein] many, of every splendid kind [of vegetation], [of every] fair species.

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:8]
Verily, in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:8]
b: Surely in that there is a sign, an indication of the perfection of His power, exalted be He; but most of them, in God’s knowledge, are not believers (kāna here according to Sībawayhi is extra).

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:9]
And verily, thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:9]
b: And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty One, Who will exact vengeance from the disbelievers, the Merciful, Who shows mercy to believers.

f:
وَإِذْ نَادَىٰ رَبُّكَ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ ائْتِ الْقَوْمَ الظَّالِمِينَ [26:10]
Behold, thy Lord called Moses عليه السلام: "Go to the people of iniquity,- [26:10]
b: And, mention, O Muhammad (s), to your people, when your Lord called to Moses عليه السلام, on the night he saw the fire and the bush, [saying]: ‘Go to the wrongdoing folk, as a messenger,

f:
قَوْمَ فِرْعَوْنَ ۚ أَلَا يَتَّقُونَ [26:11]
"The people of the Pharaoh: will they not fear Allah?" [26:11]
b: Pharaoh’s folk, to them as well as him — they wronged their souls by disbelieving in God and [wronged] the Children of Israel by enslaving them — Will they not (a-lā: the hamza indicates a negation meant as a rebuke) show fear?’, of God by being obedient to Him and affirm His Oneness?

f:
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يُكَذِّبُونِ [26:12]
He said: "O my Lord! I do fear that they will charge me with falsehood: [26:12]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, ‘My Lord, I fear they will deny me,

f:
وَيَضِيقُ صَدْرِي وَلَا يَنْطَلِقُ لِسَانِي فَأَرْسِلْ إِلَىٰ هَارُونَ [26:13]
"My breast will be straitened. And my speech may not go (smoothly): so send unto Aaron. [26:13]
b: and that anguish will constrain my breast, because of their denial of me, and that my tongue will not utter clearly, to deliver the Message, because of the knot in it. So give the Mission to, my brother, Aaron, alongside me.

f:
وَلَهُمْ عَلَيَّ ذَنْبٌ فَأَخَافُ أَنْ يَقْتُلُونِ [26:14]
"And (further), they have a charge of crime against me; and I fear they may slay me." [26:14]
b: And I have sinned against them, by my slaying of the Egyptian man, and I fear they will slay me’, for this.

f:
قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ فَاذْهَبَا بِآيَاتِنَا ۖ إِنَّا مَعَكُمْ مُسْتَمِعُونَ [26:15]
Allah said: "By no means! proceed then, both of you, with Our Signs; We are with you, and will listen (to your call). [26:15]
b: Said He, exalted be He: ‘Certainly not!, they shall not slay you. Go both of you, you and your brother — this address [although in the dual form] is predominantly for the person present as opposed to the absent one — with Our signs. We will indeed be with you, hearing, what you say and what is said to you (ma‘akum: the two [Moses عليه السلام and Aaron] are referred to here with the plural pronoun).

f:
فَأْتِيَا فِرْعَوْنَ فَقُولَا إِنَّا رَسُولُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:16]
"So go forth, both of you, to Pharaoh, and say: ´We have been sent by the Lord and Cherisher of the worlds; [26:16]
b: So the two of you approach Pharaoh and say, “Indeed We are — [indeed] each of the two of us is, the Messenger of the Lord of the Worlds, to you,

f:
أَنْ أَرْسِلْ مَعَنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ [26:17]
"´Send thou with us the Children of Israel.´" [26:17]
b: that you should let go forth with us, to Syria, the Children of Israel” ’. So they approached him and said to him that which has been mentioned.

f:
قَالَ أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا وَلَبِثْتَ فِينَا مِنْ عُمُرِكَ سِنِينَ [26:18]
(Pharaoh) said: "Did we not cherish thee as a child among us, and didst thou not stay in our midst many years of thy life? [26:18]
b: He, Pharaoh, said, to Moses عليه السلام, ‘Did we not rear you among us, in our homes, as a child?, as an infant, only recently born but weaned, and did you not stay with us for years of your life?, for thirty years — he would dress from Pharaoh’s clothes and ride chariots of his, and was referred to as Pharaoh’s son.

f:
وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلَتَكَ الَّتِي فَعَلْتَ وَأَنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ [26:19]
"And thou didst a deed of thine which (thou knowest) thou didst, and thou art an ungrateful (wretch)!" [26:19]
b: And you committed that deed of yours — namely, his slaying of the Egyptian — being an ingrate’, a denier of my favours to you in having reared you [among us] and not enslaved you.

f:
قَالَ فَعَلْتُهَا إِذًا وَأَنَا مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ [26:20]
Moses عليه السلام said: "I did it then, when I was in error. [26:20]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, ‘I did that then, when I was astray, from the knowledge and the Message which God would later give me.

f:
فَفَرَرْتُ مِنْكُمْ لَمَّا خِفْتُكُمْ فَوَهَبَ لِي رَبِّي حُكْمًا وَجَعَلَنِي مِنَ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:21]
"So I fled from you (all) when I feared you; but my Lord has (since) invested me with judgment (and wisdom) and appointed me as one of the messengers. [26:21]
b: So I fled from you, as I was afraid of you. Then my Lord gave me judgement, knowledge, and made me one of the messengers.

f:
وَتِلْكَ نِعْمَةٌ تَمُنُّهَا عَلَيَّ أَنْ عَبَّدْتَ بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ [26:22]
"And this is the favour with which thou dost reproach me,- that thou hast enslaved the Children of Israel!" [26:22]
b: That is a favour with which you now reproach me that you have enslaved the Children of Israel’ (an ‘abbadta banī Isrā’īl, is explicative of tilka, ‘that’) in other words, you have enslaved them but not me: there is no favour in that, for your enslavement of them is wrong (some [scholars] have reckoned there to be an interrogative hamza of denial at the beginning of this verse [a-tilka ni‘matun, ‘is that a favour?’]).

f:
قَالَ فِرْعَوْنُ وَمَا رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:23]
Pharaoh said: "And what is the ´Lord and Cherisher of the worlds´?" [26:23]
b: Pharaoh said, to Moses عليه السلام, ‘And what is “the Lord of the Worlds” ’, the One Whose Messenger you say you indeed are? In other words: what exactly is He? And since there is no way for creation to know the true nature of God, but only to know Him through [an articulation of] His attributes, Moses, blessings and peace be upon him, responds to him with [mention of] some of these [attributes]:

f:
قَالَ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ مُوقِنِينَ [26:24]
(Moses) said: "The Lord and Cherisher of the heavens and the earth, and all between,- if ye want to be quite sure." [26:24]
b: He said, ‘The Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, in other words, the Creator of [all] that — should you have conviction’, that He, exalted be He, is their Creator, then believe in Him alone.

f:
قَالَ لِمَنْ حَوْلَهُ أَلَا تَسْتَمِعُونَ [26:25]
(Pharaoh) said to those around: "Did ye not listen (to what he says)?" [26:25]
b: He, Pharaoh, said to those, noblemen among his folk, who were around him, ‘Did you not hear?!’, his response, how it does not correspond to the question [I asked]?

f:
قَالَ رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمُ الْأَوَّلِينَ [26:26]
(Moses) said: "Your Lord and the Lord of your fathers from the beginning!" [26:26]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, ‘Your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers’. Now, even though this [fact] is comprised by what was [said] before it enrages Pharaoh, and therefore:

f:
قَالَ إِنَّ رَسُولَكُمُ الَّذِي أُرْسِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ لَمَجْنُونٌ [26:27]
(Pharaoh) said: "Truly your messenger who has been sent to you is a veritable madman!" [26:27]
b: He said, ‘Verily this messenger of yours sent to you is a madman!’

f:
قَالَ رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ [26:28]
(Moses) said: "Lord of the East and the West, and all between! if ye only had sense!" [26:28]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, ‘The Lord of the east and the west and all that is between them — should you comprehend,’, that He is such [a Lord] then believe in Him alone.

f:
قَالَ لَئِنِ اتَّخَذْتَ إِلَٰهًا غَيْرِي لَأَجْعَلَنَّكَ مِنَ الْمَسْجُونِينَ [26:29]
(Pharaoh) said: "If thou dost put forward any god other than me, I will certainly put thee in prison!" [26:29]
b: He, Pharaoh, said, to Moses عليه السلام: ‘If you choose any god other than me, I will surely make you a prisoner!’. His [Pharaoh’s] prison was very harsh, for a person would be shut up [in a dungeon] underground alone, where he could neither see nor hear anyone else.

f:
قَالَ أَوَلَوْ جِئْتُكَ بِشَيْءٍ مُبِينٍ [26:30]
(Moses) said: "Even if I showed you something clear (and) convincing?" [26:30]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, to him: ‘What, would you do this even, if I bring you something manifest?’, patent proof of my Mission?

f:
قَالَ فَأْتِ بِهِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ [26:31]
(Pharaoh) said: "Show it then, if thou tellest the truth!" [26:31]
b: He, Pharaoh, said, to him: ‘Then bring it, if you are truthful’, in this.

f:
فَأَلْقَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ ثُعْبَانٌ مُبِينٌ [26:32]
So (Moses) threw his rod, and behold, it was a serpent, plain (for all to see)! [26:32]
b: So he threw down his staff, and lo! it was a manifest serpent, a great snake.

f:
وَنَزَعَ يَدَهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ بَيْضَاءُ لِلنَّاظِرِينَ [26:33]
And he drew out his hand, and behold, it was white to all beholders! [26:33]
b: Then he drew out his hand, he brought it out of his pocket, and lo! it was white, glowing, before the onlookers, and not its usual skin colour.

f:
قَالَ لِلْمَلَإِ حَوْلَهُ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَسَاحِرٌ عَلِيمٌ [26:34]
(Pharaoh) said to the Chiefs around him: "This is indeed a sorcerer well-versed: [26:34]
b: He, Pharaoh, said to the council around him, ‘Surely this man is a cunning sorcerer, an expert in the art of magic,

f:
يُرِيدُ أَنْ يُخْرِجَكُمْ مِنْ أَرْضِكُمْ بِسِحْرِهِ فَمَاذَا تَأْمُرُونَ [26:35]
"His plan is to get you out of your land by his sorcery; then what is it ye counsel?" [26:35]
b: who seeks to expel you from your land by his sorcery. So what do you advise?’

f:
قَالُوا أَرْجِهْ وَأَخَاهُ وَابْعَثْ فِي الْمَدَائِنِ حَاشِرِينَ [26:36]
They said: "Keep him and his brother in suspense (for a while), and dispatch to the Cities heralds to collect- [26:36]
b: They said, ‘Put him and his brother off for a while, postpone [judgement of] their affair, and send musterers into the cities

f:
يَأْتُوكَ بِكُلِّ سَحَّارٍ عَلِيمٍ [26:37]
"And bring up to thee all (our) sorcerers well-versed." [26:37]
b: to bring you every cunning sorcerer’, to surpass Moses عليه السلام in the art of magic.

f:
فَجُمِعَ السَّحَرَةُ لِمِيقَاتِ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ [26:38]
So the sorcerers were got together for the appointment of a day well-known, [26:38]
b: So the sorcerers were assembled at a fixed time of a known day, which was the morning of the Festival Day.

f:
وَقِيلَ لِلنَّاسِ هَلْ أَنْتُمْ مُجْتَمِعُونَ [26:39]
And the people were told: "Are ye (now) assembled?- [26:39]
b: And it was said to the people, ‘Will you assemble!’

f:
لَعَلَّنَا نَتَّبِعُ السَّحَرَةَ إِنْ كَانُوا هُمُ الْغَالِبِينَ [26:40]
"That we may follow the sorcerers (in religion) if they win?" [26:40]
b: Maybe we will follow the sorcerers, should they be the victors’ (the interrogative [of the previous verse] is an incitement to assemble and the optative sense [implicit in la‘alla] is due to their anticipation of victory, and hence their continued adherence to their religion and rejection of Moses عليه السلام).

f:
فَلَمَّا جَاءَ السَّحَرَةُ قَالُوا لِفِرْعَوْنَ أَئِنَّ لَنَا لَأَجْرًا إِنْ كُنَّا نَحْنُ الْغَالِبِينَ [26:41]
So when the sorcerers arrived, they said to Pharaoh: "Of course - shall we have a (suitable) reward if we win? [26:41]
b: So when the sorcerers came, they said to Pharaoh, ‘Shall we indeed (read a-inna either by pronouncing both hamzas, or by not pronouncing the second, but in both cases inserting an alif) have a reward if we were to be the victors?’

f:
قَالَ نَعَمْ وَإِنَّكُمْ إِذًا لَمِنَ الْمُقَرَّبِينَ [26:42]
He said: "Yea, (and more),- for ye shall in that case be (raised to posts) nearest (to my person)." [26:42]
b: He said, ‘Yes [of course]! And you shall then be among those closest [to me]’.

f:
قَالَ لَهُمْ مُوسَىٰ أَلْقُوا مَا أَنْتُمْ مُلْقُونَ [26:43]
Moses عليه السلام said to them: "Throw ye - that which ye are about to throw!" [26:43]
b: Moses عليه السلام said to them, after they had said to him, Either you cast, or we shall be the casters [Q. 7:115]: ‘Cast what you have to cast’ — the command to do this signifies an authorisation for them to cast and a means whereby the truth will be made to prevail.

f:
فَأَلْقَوْا حِبَالَهُمْ وَعِصِيَّهُمْ وَقَالُوا بِعِزَّةِ فِرْعَوْنَ إِنَّا لَنَحْنُ الْغَالِبُونَ [26:44]
So they threw their ropes and their rods, and said: "By the might of Pharaoh, it is we who will certainly win!" [26:44]
b: So they cast their ropes and their staffs, and said, ‘By the power of Pharaoh we shall surely be the victors!’

f:
فَأَلْقَىٰ مُوسَىٰ عَصَاهُ فَإِذَا هِيَ تَلْقَفُ مَا يَأْفِكُونَ [26:45]
Then Moses عليه السلام threw his rod, when, behold, it straightway swallows up all the falsehoods which they fake! [26:45]
b: Thereat Moses عليه السلام cast his staff and lo! it was swallowing (talqafu: one of the original two tā’ letters [of taltaqifu] has been assimilated) what they had faked, [what they had] transformed through illusion, making their ropes and staffs appear to be moving serpents.

f:
فَأُلْقِيَ السَّحَرَةُ سَاجِدِينَ [26:46]
Then did the sorcerers fall down, prostrate in adoration, [26:46]
b: So the sorcerers fell down prostrating.

f:
قَالُوا آمَنَّا بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:47]
Saying: "We believe in the Lord of the Worlds, [26:47]
b: They said, ‘We believe in the Lord of the Worlds,

f:
رَبِّ مُوسَىٰ وَهَارُونَ [26:48]
"The Lord of Moses عليه السلام and Aaron." [26:48]
b: the Lord of Moses عليه السلام and Aaron’, for they realised that what they had witnessed in the case of the staff could not have been the result of [mere] sorcery.

f:
قَالَ آمَنْتُمْ لَهُ قَبْلَ أَنْ آذَنَ لَكُمْ ۖ إِنَّهُ لَكَبِيرُكُمُ الَّذِي عَلَّمَكُمُ السِّحْرَ فَلَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ ۚ لَأُقَطِّعَنَّ أَيْدِيَكُمْ وَأَرْجُلَكُمْ مِنْ خِلَافٍ وَلَأُصَلِّبَنَّكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ [26:49]
Said (Pharaoh): "Believe ye in Him before I give you permission? surely he is your leader, who has taught you sorcery! but soon shall ye know! Be sure I will cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will cause you all to die on the cross!" [26:49]
b: Pharaoh said, ‘Do you believe (a-āmantum, read pronouncing both hamzas or replacing the second one with an alif) him, Moses عليه السلام, though I have not given you leave? He is indeed your chief, the one who has taught you sorcery — so that he only taught you some [tricks] and then surpassed you with others. Soon you will know, what I will do with you! I will assuredly cut off your hands and legs on opposite sides — in other words, the right hand of each one together with his left leg — then I shall surely crucify you all.’

f:
قَالُوا لَا ضَيْرَ ۖ إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا مُنْقَلِبُونَ [26:50]
They said: "No matter! for us, we shall but return to our Lord! [26:50]
b: They said, ‘There is no harm [in that], no damage will be done to us thereby. Surely to our Lord, after we die, whichever way that may be, we shall return, in the Hereafter.

f:
إِنَّا نَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لَنَا رَبُّنَا خَطَايَانَا أَنْ كُنَّا أَوَّلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [26:51]
"Only, our desire is that our Lord will forgive us our faults, that we may become foremost among the believers!" [26:51]
b: Indeed We hope our Lord will forgive us our iniquities, for being the first to believe’, in our time.

f:
وَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنْ أَسْرِ بِعِبَادِي إِنَّكُمْ مُتَّبَعُونَ [26:52]
By inspiration we told Moses عليه السلام: "Travel by night with my servants; for surely ye shall be pursued." [26:52]
b: And We revealed to Moses عليه السلام, after many years which he spent among them calling them to the truth with God’s signs but all of which only increased them in insolence, [saying], ‘Journey with My servants, the Children of Israel, by night (a variant reading [for an asri] is an isr, from the verb sarā, one form of asrā) go with them by night in the direction of the sea, for indeed you will be pursued’. Pharaoh and his armies will pursue you, but when they enter the sea in pursuit of you, I will deliver you and drown them.

f:
فَأَرْسَلَ فِرْعَوْنُ فِي الْمَدَائِنِ حَاشِرِينَ [26:53]
Then Pharaoh sent heralds to (all) the Cities, [26:53]
b: Then Pharaoh, having been informed of their night departure, sent to the cities — it is said that he ruled a thousand cities and twelve thousand villages — musterers, to assemble the army, saying:

f:
إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ لَشِرْذِمَةٌ قَلِيلُونَ [26:54]
(Saying): "These (Israelites) are but a small band, [26:54]
b: ‘Lo! these are but a small gang. It is said that they [the Children of Israel] numbered 670,000, while his [Pharaoh’s] vanguard alone numbered 700,000 and so he deemed their number insignificant in comparison to his huge army.

f:
وَإِنَّهُمْ لَنَا لَغَائِظُونَ [26:55]
"And they are raging furiously against us; [26:55]
b: And indeed they have enraged us, their actions infuriate us,

f:
وَإِنَّا لَجَمِيعٌ حَاذِرُونَ [26:56]
"But we are a multitude amply fore-warned." [26:56]
b: and indeed we are all on our guard’, ready (a variant reading [for hadhirūna] has hādhirūn, meaning ‘alert’).

f:
فَأَخْرَجْنَاهُمْ مِنْ جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ [26:57]
So We expelled them from gardens, springs, [26:57]
b: God, exalted be He, says: So We made them, Pharaoh and his folk, go forth, out of Egypt, in order to pursue Moses عليه السلام and his people, from gardens, orchards on either side of the Nile, and springs, streams running from the Nile through their dwellings,

f:
وَكُنُوزٍ وَمَقَامٍ كَرِيمٍ [26:58]
Treasures, and every kind of honourable position; [26:58]
b: and treasures, visible riches of gold and silver — these [riches] are called kunūz [as opposed to amwāl, ‘riches’] because that [portion] which is [always] due to God, exalted be He, from them had not been paid — and splendid places, exquisite residences for princes and ministers surrounded by their retinues.

f:
كَذَٰلِكَ وَأَوْرَثْنَاهَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ [26:59]
Thus it was, but We made the Children of Israel inheritors of such things. [26:59]
b: So [it was], that is, Our expulsion [of them] was as We have described, and We made the Children of Israel to inherit these, after drowning Pharaoh and his folk.

f:
فَأَتْبَعُوهُمْ مُشْرِقِينَ [26:60]
So they pursued them at sunrise. [26:60]
b: Then they pursued them, they caught them up, at sunrise.

f:
فَلَمَّا تَرَاءَى الْجَمْعَانِ قَالَ أَصْحَابُ مُوسَىٰ إِنَّا لَمُدْرَكُونَ [26:61]
And when the two bodies saw each other, the people of Moses عليه السلام said: "We are sure to be overtaken." [26:61]
b: And when the two hosts sighted each other, the companions of Moses عليه السلام said, ‘We have been caught!’, Pharaoh’s hosts have caught us up and we have no power against them.

f:
قَالَ كَلَّا ۖ إِنَّ مَعِيَ رَبِّي سَيَهْدِينِ [26:62]
(Moses) said: "By no means! my Lord is with me! Soon will He guide me!" [26:62]
b: He, Moses عليه السلام, said, ‘Certainly not!, they shall not catch us up; indeed I have my Lord with me, to provide assistance. He will guide me’, to the route of deliverance.

f:
فَأَوْحَيْنَا إِلَىٰ مُوسَىٰ أَنِ اضْرِبْ بِعَصَاكَ الْبَحْرَ ۖ فَانْفَلَقَ فَكَانَ كُلُّ فِرْقٍ كَالطَّوْدِ الْعَظِيمِ [26:63]
Then We told Moses عليه السلام by inspiration: "Strike the sea with thy rod." So it divided, and each separate part became like the huge, firm mass of a mountain. [26:63]
b: God, exalted be He, says: Thereupon We revealed to Moses عليه السلام: ‘Strike the sea with your staff’, and he struck it, whereupon it parted, it split into twelve parts, and each part was as a mighty mountain, between each of these parts were paths which they followed, such that not even the saddles or the felts of the riders were touched by water.

f:
وَأَزْلَفْنَا ثَمَّ الْآخَرِينَ [26:64]
And We made the other party approach thither. [26:64]
b: And there We brought near the others, Pharaoh and his folk, until they followed them across the same paths.

f:
وَأَنْجَيْنَا مُوسَىٰ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ [26:65]
We delivered Moses عليه السلام and all who were with him; [26:65]
b: And We delivered Moses عليه السلام and all those who were with him, by bringing them out of the sea while it was in the state mentioned [above].

f:
ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا الْآخَرِينَ [26:66]
But We drowned the others. [26:66]
b: Then We drowned the others, Pharaoh and his folk by closing the sea on them after they had entered the sea and the Children of Israel had exited therefrom.

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:67]
Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:67]
b: Surely in that, drowning of Pharaoh and his folk, there is a sign, a lesson for those [generations] who would come after them; but most of them are not believers, in God. The only ones to believe were Āsiya — Pharaoh’s wife — Hizqīl, the believing man of Pharaoh’s family, and Maryam daughter of Nāmūsī, she who pointed out the bone remains of [the prophet] Joseph, peace be upon him.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:68]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:68]
b: And surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, for He wrought vengeance upon the disbelievers by drowning them, the Merciful, to believers, delivering them from drowning.

f:
وَاتْلُ عَلَيْهِمْ نَبَأَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ [26:69]
And rehearse to them (something of) Abraham عليه السلام´s story. [26:69]
b: And recite to them, the disbelievers of Mecca, the tiding, the tale, of Abraham عليه السلام (Ibrāhīma is substituted by [the following, idh qāla, ‘when he said’])

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لِأَبِيهِ وَقَوْمِهِ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ [26:70]
Behold, he said to his father and his people: "What worship ye?" [26:70]
b: when he said to his father and his people, ‘What do you worship?’

f:
قَالُوا نَعْبُدُ أَصْنَامًا فَنَظَلُّ لَهَا عَاكِفِينَ [26:71]
They said: "We worship idols, and we remain constantly in attendance on them." [26:71]
b: They said, ‘We worship idols — they reiterate the verb [in the response] in order to supplement it with [the following remark] — and remain cleaving to them’, we remain worshipping them all day; they give a longer response to indicate their [misplaced] pride in such [an act].

f:
قَالَ هَلْ يَسْمَعُونَكُمْ إِذْ تَدْعُونَ [26:72]
He said: "Do they listen to you when ye call (on them)?" [26:72]
b: He said, ‘Do they hear you when you supplicate?

f:
أَوْ يَنْفَعُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَضُرُّونَ [26:73]
"Or do you good or harm?" [26:73]
b: Or do they bring you benefit, when you worship them, or harm?, to you, if you do not?

f:
قَالُوا بَلْ وَجَدْنَا آبَاءَنَا كَذَٰلِكَ يَفْعَلُونَ [26:74]
They said: "Nay, but we found our fathers doing thus (what we do)." [26:74]
b: They said, ‘Rather, we found our fathers so doing’, that is, doing the same as we do.

f:
قَالَ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ [26:75]
He said: "Do ye then see whom ye have been worshipping,- [26:75]
b: He said, ‘Have you considered what you have been worshipping,

f:
أَنْتُمْ وَآبَاؤُكُمُ الْأَقْدَمُونَ [26:76]
"Ye and your fathers before you?- [26:76]
b: you and your ancestors?

f:
فَإِنَّهُمْ عَدُوٌّ لِي إِلَّا رَبَّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:77]
"For they are enemies to me; not so the Lord and Cherisher of the Worlds; [26:77]
b: They are indeed hateful to me, I do not worship them; but the Lord of the Worlds, I do worship Him,

f:
الَّذِي خَلَقَنِي فَهُوَ يَهْدِينِ [26:78]
"Who created me, and it is He Who guides me; [26:78]
b: [He] Who created me, it is He Who guides me, to [the proper] religion,

f:
وَالَّذِي هُوَ يُطْعِمُنِي وَيَسْقِينِ [26:79]
"Who gives me food and drink, [26:79]
b: and provides me with food and drink,

f:
وَإِذَا مَرِضْتُ فَهُوَ يَشْفِينِ [26:80]
"And when I am ill, it is He Who cures me; [26:80]
b: and when I am sick, it is He Who cures me;

f:
وَالَّذِي يُمِيتُنِي ثُمَّ يُحْيِينِ [26:81]
"Who will cause me to die, and then to life (again); [26:81]
b: and Who will make me die, then give me life,

f:
وَالَّذِي أَطْمَعُ أَنْ يَغْفِرَ لِي خَطِيئَتِي يَوْمَ الدِّينِ [26:82]
"And who, I hope, will forgive me my faults on the day of Judgment. [26:82]
b: and Who, I hope, will forgive me my iniquity on the Day of Judgement, [the Day] of Requital.

f:
رَبِّ هَبْ لِي حُكْمًا وَأَلْحِقْنِي بِالصَّالِحِينَ [26:83]
"O my Lord! bestow wisdom on me, and join me with the righteous; [26:83]
b: My Lord! Grant me [unerring] judgement, knowledge, and unite me with the righteous, the prophets.

f:
وَاجْعَلْ لِي لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِي الْآخِرِينَ [26:84]
"Grant me honourable mention on the tongue of truth among the latest (generations); [26:84]
b: And confer on me a worthy repute, excellent praise, among posterity, those who will come after me up to the Day of Resurrection.

f:
وَاجْعَلْنِي مِنْ وَرَثَةِ جَنَّةِ النَّعِيمِ [26:85]
"Make me one of the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss; [26:85]
b: And make me among the inheritors of the Garden of Bliss, among those who will be given it.

f:
وَاغْفِرْ لِأَبِي إِنَّهُ كَانَ مِنَ الضَّالِّينَ [26:86]
"Forgive my father, for that he is among those astray; [26:86]
b: And forgive my father, for indeed he is one of those who are astray, by Your relenting to him and forgiving him: this was before it became clear to him [Abraham عليه السلام] that he [his father] was an enemy of God, as mentioned in sūrat Barā’a [Q. 9:114].

f:
وَلَا تُخْزِنِي يَوْمَ يُبْعَثُونَ [26:87]
"And let me not be in disgrace on the Day when (men) will be raised up;- [26:87]
b: And do not disgrace me, do not expose me, on the day when they, mankind, are resurrected;

f:
يَوْمَ لَا يَنْفَعُ مَالٌ وَلَا بَنُونَ [26:88]
"The Day whereon neither wealth nor sons will avail, [26:88]
b: of which [day] God, exalted be He, says [the following]: the day when neither wealth nor children will avail, anyone,

f:
إِلَّا مَنْ أَتَى اللَّهَ بِقَلْبٍ سَلِيمٍ [26:89]
"But only he (will prosper) that brings to Allah a sound heart; [26:89]
b: except him who comes to God with a heart that is sound, [free] from idolatry and hypocrisy — and this is the heart of the believer, whom such [things] will avail.

f:
وَأُزْلِفَتِ الْجَنَّةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ [26:90]
"To the righteous, the Garden will be brought near, [26:90]
b: And Paradise will be brought near for the God-fearing, and they will [be able to] see it,

f:
وَبُرِّزَتِ الْجَحِيمُ لِلْغَاوِينَ [26:91]
"And to those straying in Evil, the Fire will be placed in full view; [26:91]
b: and Hell will be revealed [plainly] for the perverse, the disbelievers.

f:
وَقِيلَ لَهُمْ أَيْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْبُدُونَ [26:92]
"And it shall be said to them: ´Where are the (gods) ye worshipped- [26:92]
b: And it will be said to them, ‘Where is that which you used to worship

f:
مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ هَلْ يَنْصُرُونَكُمْ أَوْ يَنْتَصِرُونَ [26:93]
"´Besides Allah? Can they help you or help themselves?´ [26:93]
b: besides God?, that is, other than Him, in the way of idols. Do they help you, by averting from you the chastisement, or do they help one another?’, by averting it from themselves? No [neither]!

f:
فَكُبْكِبُوا فِيهَا هُمْ وَالْغَاوُونَ [26:94]
"Then they will be thrown headlong into the (Fire),- they and those straying in Evil, [26:94]
b: Then they will be hurled, cast, into it, they and the perverse,

f:
وَجُنُودُ إِبْلِيسَ أَجْمَعُونَ [26:95]
"And the whole hosts of Iblis together. [26:95]
b: and the hosts of Iblīs, his followers and those jinn and humans who were obedient to him, all together.

f:
قَالُوا وَهُمْ فِيهَا يَخْتَصِمُونَ [26:96]
"They will say there in their mutual bickerings: [26:96]
b: They, the perverse, shall say, as they wrangle therein, with those whom they used to worship:

f:
تَاللَّهِ إِنْ كُنَّا لَفِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ [26:97]
"´By Allah, we were truly in an error manifest, [26:97]
b: ‘By God, we had indeed (in, softened in place of the hardened form, with its subject omitted, in other words [it would usually be] innahu) been in manifest error,

f:
إِذْ نُسَوِّيكُمْ بِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:98]
"´When we held you as equals with the Lord of the Worlds; [26:98]
b: when we equated you, in worship, with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
وَمَا أَضَلَّنَا إِلَّا الْمُجْرِمُونَ [26:99]
"´And our seducers were only those who were steeped in guilt. [26:99]
b: And it was none other than the sinners, the devils or our predecessors, whose example we were following, that led us astray, from guidance.

f:
فَمَا لَنَا مِنْ شَافِعِينَ [26:100]
"´Now, then, we have none to intercede (for us), [26:100]
b: So [now] we have no intercessors, as the believers have, in the way of angels, prophets and [other] believers,

f:
وَلَا صَدِيقٍ حَمِيمٍ [26:101]
"´Nor a single friend to feel (for us). [26:101]
b: nor any sympathetic friend, who might be concerned for us.

f:
فَلَوْ أَنَّ لَنَا كَرَّةً فَنَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [26:102]
"´Now if we only had a chance of return we shall truly be of those who believe!´" [26:102]
b: If only we had another turn, [another] return to this world, we would have been among those who believe!’ (law, ‘if only’, here is for [the conditional] optative, to which nakūna, ‘we would have been’, constitutes the response).

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:103]
Verily in this is a Sign but most of them do not believe. [26:103]
b: Surely in that, which is mentioned of the tale of Abraham عليه السلام and his people, there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:104]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:104]
b: And truly your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:105]
The people of Noah عليه السلام rejected the messengers. [26:105]
b: The people of Noah عليه السلام denied the messengers, by denying him, for they all brought the same message affirming God’s Oneness; or [it is] because he stayed among them for so long that it was as though he was many messengers (the feminine [person of the verb kadhdhabat, ‘denied’, governed by] qawm, ‘the people’, is on account of the import, but it is masculine on account of its [morphological] form);

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ نُوحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ [26:106]
Behold, their brother Noah عليه السلام said to them: "Will ye not fear (Allah)? [26:106]
b: when Noah عليه السلام, their brother — [their brother only] in terms of lineage — said to them, ‘Will you not fear?, God?

f:
إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ [26:107]
"I am to you a messenger worthy of all trust: [26:107]
b: Truly I am a trusted messenger [sent] to you, to deliver the Message with which I have been sent.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:108]
"So fear Allah, and obey me. [26:108]
b: So fear God and obey me, in what I enjoin you to of God’s Oneness and obedience to Him.

f:
وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:109]
"No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the Lord of the Worlds: [26:109]
b: I do not ask of you any reward for it, for delivering it; for my reward lies only with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:110]
"So fear Allah, and obey me." [26:110]
b: So fear God and obey me’ — he repeats this [statement] for emphasis.

f:
قَالُوا أَنُؤْمِنُ لَكَ وَاتَّبَعَكَ الْأَرْذَلُونَ [26:111]
They said: "Shall we believe in thee when it is the meanest that follow thee?" [26:111]
b: They said, ‘Shall we believe in you, in your words, when it is the lowliest people who follow you?’ (wa’ttaba‘aka: a variant reading has wa-atbā‘uka, ‘[when] your followers’, plural of tābi‘, ‘follower’, as a subject) the riffraff, such as the weavers and the shoemakers.

f:
قَالَ وَمَا عِلْمِي بِمَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ [26:112]
He said: "And what do I know as to what they do? [26:112]
b: He said, ‘And what do I know of what they may have been doing?

f:
إِنْ حِسَابُهُمْ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّي ۖ لَوْ تَشْعُرُونَ [26:113]
"Their account is only with my Lord, if ye could (but) understand. [26:113]
b: Their reckoning is only my Lord’s concern, and He will requite them, if only you were aware — had you known this, you would not have reviled them.

f:
وَمَا أَنَا بِطَارِدِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [26:114]
"I am not one to drive away those who believe. [26:114]
b: And I am not about to drive away the believers.

f:
إِنْ أَنَا إِلَّا نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ [26:115]
"I am sent only to warn plainly in public." [26:115]
b: I am just a plain warner’.

f:
قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يَا نُوحُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمَرْجُومِينَ [26:116]
They said: "If thou desist not, O Noah عليه السلام! thou shalt be stoned (to death)." [26:116]
b: They said, ‘Lo! if you do not desist, O Noah عليه السلام, from what you say to us, you will assuredly be among those assailed’, with stones or curses.

f:
قَالَ رَبِّ إِنَّ قَوْمِي كَذَّبُونِ [26:117]
He said: "O my Lord! truly my people have rejected me. [26:117]
b: He, Noah عليه السلام, said, ‘My Lord, my people have denied me,

f:
فَافْتَحْ بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَهُمْ فَتْحًا وَنَجِّنِي وَمَنْ مَعِيَ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ [26:118]
"Judge Thou, then, between me and them openly, and deliver me and those of the Believers who are with me." [26:118]
b: so judge conclusively between me and them, and deliver me and the believers who are with me’.

f:
فَأَنْجَيْنَاهُ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ فِي الْفُلْكِ الْمَشْحُونِ [26:119]
So We delivered him and those with him, in the Ark filled (with all creatures). [26:119]
b: He, exalted be He, says: So We delivered him and those who were with him in the laden ark, [the ship] filled with humans, animals and birds.

f:
ثُمَّ أَغْرَقْنَا بَعْدُ الْبَاقِينَ [26:120]
Thereafter We drowned those who remained behind. [26:120]
b: Then afterwards, after We delivered them, We drowned the rest, of his people.

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:121]
Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:121]
b: Surely in that there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:122]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:122]
b: Truly your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
كَذَّبَتْ عَادٌ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:123]
The ´Ad (people) rejected the messengers. [26:123]
b: ‘Ād denied the messengers,

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ هُودٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ [26:124]
Behold, their brother Hud said to them: "Will ye not fear (Allah)? [26:124]
b: when Hūd, their brother, said to them, ‘Will you not fear God?

f:
إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ [26:125]
"I am to you a messenger worthy of all trust: [26:125]
b: Truly I am a trusted messenger [sent] to you.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:126]
"So fear Allah and obey me. [26:126]
b: So fear God and obey me.

f:
وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:127]
"No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the Lord of the Worlds. [26:127]
b: I do not ask of you any reward for this; for my reward lies only with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
أَتَبْنُونَ بِكُلِّ رِيعٍ آيَةً تَعْبَثُونَ [26:128]
"Do ye build a landmark on every high place to amuse yourselves? [26:128]
b: Do you build on every prominence, every high place, a monument, an edifice as a signpost for passers-by, so that you may hurl abuse?, at those who pass by you and deride them (ta‘bathūna, is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of [the verb] tabnūna, ‘you build’).

f:
وَتَتَّخِذُونَ مَصَانِعَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَخْلُدُونَ [26:129]
"And do ye get for yourselves fine buildings in the hope of living therein (for ever)? [26:129]
b: And you set up structures, for [extracting] water underground, that perhaps you might, as though you will, last forever, therein and not die.

f:
وَإِذَا بَطَشْتُمْ بَطَشْتُمْ جَبَّارِينَ [26:130]
"And when ye exert your strong hand, do ye do it like men of absolute power? [26:130]
b: And when you assault, to smite or slay, you assault like tyrants, mercilessly!

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:131]
"Now fear Allah, and obey me. [26:131]
b: So fear God, in this, and obey me, in what I have commanded you.

f:
وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي أَمَدَّكُمْ بِمَا تَعْلَمُونَ [26:132]
"Yea, fear Him Who has bestowed on you freely all that ye know. [26:132]
b: And fear Him Who has provided you, Who has been gracious to you, in a way that you know,

f:
أَمَدَّكُمْ بِأَنْعَامٍ وَبَنِينَ [26:133]
"Freely has He bestowed on you cattle and sons,- [26:133]
b: provided you with cattle and sons,

f:
وَجَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ [26:134]
"And Gardens and Springs. [26:134]
b: and gardens, orchards, and springs, rivers.

f:
إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ [26:135]
"Truly I fear for you the Penalty of a Great Day." [26:135]
b: Indeed I fear for you the chastisement of a tremendous day’, in this world and in the Hereafter should you disobey me.

f:
قَالُوا سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا أَوَعَظْتَ أَمْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنَ الْوَاعِظِينَ [26:136]
They said: "It is the same to us whether thou admonish us or be not among (our) admonishers! [26:136]
b: They said, ‘It is the same to us whether you admonish [us] or are not one of those who admonish, anyway. In other words, we will not heed your admonition.

f:
إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا خُلُقُ الْأَوَّلِينَ [26:137]
"This is no other than a customary device of the ancients, [26:137]
b: This, that you threaten us with, is merely the fabrication of the ancients, that is, their inventions and lies (a variant reading [for khalq, ‘fabrication’] is khuluq, ‘ethos’, in other words, this denial of resurrection to which we adhere is merely ‘the ethos of the ancients’, in other words, their nature and wont);

f:
وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمُعَذَّبِينَ [26:138]
"And we are not the ones to receive Pains and Penalties!" [26:138]
b: and we will not be chastised’.

f:
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَهْلَكْنَاهُمْ ۗ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:139]
So they rejected him, and We destroyed them. Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:139]
b: So they denied him, concerning the chastisement, whereupon We destroyed them, in this world with the [barren] wind [cf. Q. 51:41]. Surely in that there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:140]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:140]
b: Truly your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
كَذَّبَتْ ثَمُودُ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:141]
The Thamud (people) rejected the messengers. [26:141]
b: Thamūd denied the messengers,

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ صَالِحٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ [26:142]
Behold, their brother Salih said to them: "Will you not fear (Allah)? [26:142]
b: when Sālih, their brother, said to them, ‘Will you fear God?

f:
إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ [26:143]
"I am to you a messenger worthy of all trust. [26:143]
b: Truly I am a trusted messenger [sent] to you.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:144]
"So fear Allah, and obey me. [26:144]
b: So fear God and obey me.

f:
وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:145]
"No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the Lord of the Worlds. [26:145]
b: I do not ask of you any reward for this; for my reward lies only with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
أَتُتْرَكُونَ فِي مَا هَاهُنَا آمِنِينَ [26:146]
"Will ye be left secure, in (the enjoyment of) all that ye have here?- [26:146]
b: Will you be left secure in that which is here, of good things —

f:
فِي جَنَّاتٍ وَعُيُونٍ [26:147]
"Gardens and Springs, [26:147]
b: amid gardens and springs,

f:
وَزُرُوعٍ وَنَخْلٍ طَلْعُهَا هَضِيمٌ [26:148]
"And corn-fields and date-palms with spathes near breaking (with the weight of fruit)? [26:148]
b: and farms and date palms with slender, delicate and tender, spathes?

f:
وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَارِهِينَ [26:149]
"And ye carve houses out of (rocky) mountains with great skill. [26:149]
b: And you hew dwellings out of the mountains arrogantly (a variant reading [of farihīna, ‘arrogant’] has fārihīn, ‘skilfully’).

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:150]
"But fear Allah and obey me; [26:150]
b: So fear God and obey me, in what I have commanded you,

f:
وَلَا تُطِيعُوا أَمْرَ الْمُسْرِفِينَ [26:151]
"And follow not the bidding of those who are extravagant,- [26:151]
b: and do not obey the command of the prodigal,

f:
الَّذِينَ يُفْسِدُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا يُصْلِحُونَ [26:152]
"Who make mischief in the land, and mend not (their ways)." [26:152]
b: who cause corruption in the earth, through acts of disobedience, and act righteously’, by being obedient to God.

f:
قَالُوا إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ [26:153]
They said: "Thou art only one of those bewitched! [26:153]
b: They said, ‘You are indeed one of the bewitched, those who have succumbed so many times to sorcery that their minds have been overcome.

f:
مَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا فَأْتِ بِآيَةٍ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ [26:154]
"Thou art no more than a mortal like us: then bring us a Sign, if thou tellest the truth!" [26:154]
b: And, moreover, you are just a human being like us. So bring [us] a sign, if you are sincere’, in your Mission.

f:
قَالَ هَٰذِهِ نَاقَةٌ لَهَا شِرْبٌ وَلَكُمْ شِرْبُ يَوْمٍ مَعْلُومٍ [26:155]
He said: "Here is a she-camel: she has a right of watering, and ye have a right of watering, (severally) on a day appointed. [26:155]
b: He said, ‘This is a she-camel; she shall drink, a share of the water, and you shall drink [each] on a known day.

f:
وَلَا تَمَسُّوهَا بِسُوءٍ فَيَأْخُذَكُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ [26:156]
"Touch her not with harm, lest the Penalty of a Great Day seize you." [26:156]
b: And do not cause her any harm, for then you shall be seized by the chastisement of an awful day’, [awful] because of the awfulness of the chastisement.

f:
فَعَقَرُوهَا فَأَصْبَحُوا نَادِمِينَ [26:157]
But they ham-strung her: then did they become full of regrets. [26:157]
b: But they hamstrung her — a group of them hamstrung her with the approval of others; and then became remorseful, for having hamstrung it.

f:
فَأَخَذَهُمُ الْعَذَابُ ۗ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:158]
But the Penalty seized them. Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:158]
b: So they were seized by the chastisement, which had been promised and were destroyed. Surely in that there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:159]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:159]
b: Truly your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
كَذَّبَتْ قَوْمُ لُوطٍ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:160]
The people of Lut rejected the messengers. [26:160]
b: The people of Lot denied the messengers,

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ أَخُوهُمْ لُوطٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ [26:161]
Behold, their brother Lut said to them: "Will ye not fear (Allah)? [26:161]
b: when Lot, their brother, said to them, ‘Will you not fear God?

f:
إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ [26:162]
"I am to you a messenger worthy of all trust. [26:162]
b: Truly I am a trusted messenger [sent] to you.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:163]
"So fear Allah and obey me. [26:163]
b: So fear God and obey me.

f:
وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:164]
"No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the lord of the Worlds. [26:164]
b: I do not ask of you any reward for this; my reward lies only with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
أَتَأْتُونَ الذُّكْرَانَ مِنَ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:165]
"Of all the creatures in the world, will ye approach males, [26:165]
b: What! Of all people you come unto males [to fornicate],

f:
وَتَذَرُونَ مَا خَلَقَ لَكُمْ رَبُّكُمْ مِنْ أَزْوَاجِكُمْ ۚ بَلْ أَنْتُمْ قَوْمٌ عَادُونَ [26:166]
"And leave those whom Allah has created for you to be your mates? Nay, ye are a people transgressing (all limits)!" [26:166]
b: and forsake the wives your Lord has created for you?, in other words, [you forsake intimacy with] their front parts? Nay, but you are a transgressing folk’, overstepping [the bounds of] what is lawful into what is unlawful.

f:
قَالُوا لَئِنْ لَمْ تَنْتَهِ يَا لُوطُ لَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْمُخْرَجِينَ [26:167]
They said: "If thou desist not, O Lut! thou wilt assuredly be cast out!" [26:167]
b: They said, ‘If you do not desist, O Lot, from reproaching us, you will assuredly be of those expelled’, from our land.

f:
قَالَ إِنِّي لِعَمَلِكُمْ مِنَ الْقَالِينَ [26:168]
He said: "I do detest your doings." [26:168]
b: He, Lot, said, ‘Truly I abhor, I detest, what you do.

f:
رَبِّ نَجِّنِي وَأَهْلِي مِمَّا يَعْمَلُونَ [26:169]
"O my Lord! deliver me and my family from such things as they do!" [26:169]
b: My Lord, deliver me and my family from what they do’, that is, from the punishment for it.

f:
فَنَجَّيْنَاهُ وَأَهْلَهُ أَجْمَعِينَ [26:170]
So We delivered him and his family,- all [26:170]
b: So We delivered him and all his family,

f:
إِلَّا عَجُوزًا فِي الْغَابِرِينَ [26:171]
Except an old woman who lingered behind. [26:171]
b: except an old woman — his wife — among those who stayed behind, whom We destroyed.

f:
ثُمَّ دَمَّرْنَا الْآخَرِينَ [26:172]
But the rest We destroyed utterly. [26:172]
b: Then We destroyed [all] the others,

f:
وَأَمْطَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ مَطَرًا ۖ فَسَاءَ مَطَرُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ [26:173]
We rained down on them a shower (of brimstone): and evil was the shower on those who were admonished (but heeded not)! [26:173]
b: and We rained on them a rain, [We rained on them] stones — this [detail] pertains to [the previous] statement concerning their destruction — and evil was, their rain, the rain of those who were warned!

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:174]
Verily in this is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:174]
b: Surely in that there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:175]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might Most Merciful. [26:175]
b: Surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
كَذَّبَ أَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ الْمُرْسَلِينَ [26:176]
The Companions of the Wood rejected the messengers. [26:176]
b: The dwellers in the wood (a variant reading [for ashābu’l-aykati] has ashābu laykata), a thicket of trees near Midian, denied the messengers,

f:
إِذْ قَالَ لَهُمْ شُعَيْبٌ أَلَا تَتَّقُونَ [26:177]
Behold, Shu´aib said to them: "Will ye not fear (Allah)? [26:177]
b: when Shu‘ayb — He [God] does not say ‘their brother’ [in this instance] because he [Shu‘ayb] was not [in terms of lineage] one of them — said to them, ‘Will you not fear God?

f:
إِنِّي لَكُمْ رَسُولٌ أَمِينٌ [26:178]
"I am to you a messenger worthy of all trust. [26:178]
b: Truly I am a trusted messenger [sent] to you.

f:
فَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ [26:179]
"So fear Allah and obey me. [26:179]
b: So fear God and obey me.

f:
وَمَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۖ إِنْ أَجْرِيَ إِلَّا عَلَىٰ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:180]
"No reward do I ask of you for it: my reward is only from the Lord of the Worlds. [26:180]
b: I do not ask of you any reward for this; indeed my reward lies only with the Lord of the Worlds.

f:
أَوْفُوا الْكَيْلَ وَلَا تَكُونُوا مِنَ الْمُخْسِرِينَ [26:181]
"Give just measure, and cause no loss (to others by fraud). [26:181]
b: Give full measure and do not be of those who give short measure,

f:
وَزِنُوا بِالْقِسْطَاسِ الْمُسْتَقِيمِ [26:182]
"And weigh with scales true and upright. [26:182]
b: and weigh with an even balance,

f:
وَلَا تَبْخَسُوا النَّاسَ أَشْيَاءَهُمْ وَلَا تَعْثَوْا فِي الْأَرْضِ مُفْسِدِينَ [26:183]
"And withhold not things justly due to men, nor do evil in the land, working mischief. [26:183]
b: and do not defraud people in their goods, do not diminish anything of what is due to them, and do not be degenerate in the earth, seeking corruption, by killing or otherwise ([ta‘thaw, ‘degenerate’] derives from ‘athiya, meaning afsada, ‘to corrupt’; mufsidīna, ‘seeking corruption’, is a circumstantial qualifier emphasising the import of its operator [ta‘thaw]).

f:
وَاتَّقُوا الَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ وَالْجِبِلَّةَ الْأَوَّلِينَ [26:184]
"And fear Him Who created you and (who created) the generations before (you)" [26:184]
b: And fear Him Who created you and the former generations’, [all] creation [before you].

f:
قَالُوا إِنَّمَا أَنْتَ مِنَ الْمُسَحَّرِينَ [26:185]
They said: "Thou art only one of those bewitched! [26:185]
b: They said, ‘You are indeed one of the bewitched.

f:
وَمَا أَنْتَ إِلَّا بَشَرٌ مِثْلُنَا وَإِنْ نَظُنُّكَ لَمِنَ الْكَاذِبِينَ [26:186]
"Thou art no more than a mortal like us, and indeed we think thou art a liar! [26:186]
b: You are just a human being like us. And we indeed (in, softened in place of the hardened form, its subject omitted, in other words [it would be] innahu) think that you are one of the liars.

f:
فَأَسْقِطْ عَلَيْنَا كِسَفًا مِنَ السَّمَاءِ إِنْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الصَّادِقِينَ [26:187]
"Now cause a piece of the sky to fall on us, if thou art truthful!" [26:187]
b: Then make fragments (read kisfan or kisafan) of the heaven fall upon us, if you are of the truthful’, in your Mission.

f:
قَالَ رَبِّي أَعْلَمُ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ [26:188]
He said: "My Lord knows best what ye do." [26:188]
b: He said, ‘My Lord knows best what you are doing’, and will requite you for it.

f:
فَكَذَّبُوهُ فَأَخَذَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمِ الظُّلَّةِ ۚ إِنَّهُ كَانَ عَذَابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ [26:189]
But they rejected him. Then the punishment of a day of overshadowing gloom seized them, and that was the Penalty of a Great Day. [26:189]
b: But they denied him, so they were seized by the chastisement of the day of the shade (al-zulla) — a cloud which gave them shade when they suffered a bout of extreme heat but which then rained down fire on them and they were incinerated. Assuredly it was the chastisement of a tremendous day.

f:
إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَةً ۖ وَمَا كَانَ أَكْثَرُهُمْ مُؤْمِنِينَ [26:190]
Verily in that is a Sign: but most of them do not believe. [26:190]
b: Surely in that there is a sign; but most of them are not believers.

f:
وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ [26:191]
And verily thy Lord is He, the Exalted in Might, Most Merciful. [26:191]
b: Surely your Lord, He is the Mighty, the Merciful.

f:
وَإِنَّهُ لَتَنْزِيلُ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ [26:192]
Verily this is a Revelation from the Lord of the Worlds: [26:192]
b: Truly it, the Qur’ān, is the revelation of the Lord of the Worlds,

f:
نَزَلَ بِهِ الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ [26:193]
