وَاللَّهُ أَنْبَتَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا [71:17]
"´And Allah has produced you from the earth growing (gradually), [71:17]
b: And God has caused you to grow, He has created you, from the earth, for He created your father Adam عليه السلام from it.

f:
ثُمَّ يُعِيدُكُمْ فِيهَا وَيُخْرِجُكُمْ إِخْرَاجًا [71:18]
"´And in the End He will return you into the (earth), and raise you forth (again at the Resurrection)? [71:18]
b: Then He will make you return into it, entombed [in your graves], and bring you forth, for the resurrection, [with a veritable bringing forth].

f:
وَاللَّهُ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ الْأَرْضَ بِسَاطًا [71:19]
"´And Allah has made the earth for you as a carpet (spread out), [71:19]
b: And God has made the earth a flat [open] expanse for you,

f:
لِتَسْلُكُوا مِنْهَا سُبُلًا فِجَاجًا [71:20]
"´That ye may go about therein, in spacious roads.´" [71:20]
b: so that you may follow throughout it spacious routes.” ’

f:
قَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ إِنَّهُمْ عَصَوْنِي وَاتَّبَعُوا مَنْ لَمْ يَزِدْهُ مَالُهُ وَوَلَدُهُ إِلَّا خَسَارًا [71:21]
Noah عليه السلام said: "O my Lord! They have disobeyed me, but they follow (men) whose wealth and children give them no increase but only Loss. [71:21]
b: Noah عليه السلام said, ‘My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed, that is, the riffraff and the paupers [among them have followed], those whose wealth and children, namely, their leaders who have been blessed with such things (read wulduhu or waladuhu, ‘whose children’, the first of which is said to be the plural of walad, similar [in pattern] to khasab, khushb, or in fact [it is said to be] of the same meaning [as walad, but an alternative form] as in the case of bukhl or bakhal, ‘niggardliness’), only add to their loss, [to] their insolence and disbelief.

f:
وَمَكَرُوا مَكْرًا كُبَّارًا [71:22]
"And they have devised a tremendous Plot. [71:22]
b: And they have devised, namely, the leaders, a mighty plot, extremely outrageous, by denying Noah عليه السلام and harming him as well as his followers,

f:
وَقَالُوا لَا تَذَرُنَّ آلِهَتَكُمْ وَلَا تَذَرُنَّ وَدًّا وَلَا سُوَاعًا وَلَا يَغُوثَ وَيَعُوقَ وَنَسْرًا [71:23]
"And they have said (to each other), ´Abandon not your gods: Abandon neither Wadd nor Suwa´, neither Yaguth nor Ya´uq, nor Nasr´;- [71:23]
b: and have said, to the riffraff: “Do not abandon your gods, and do not abandon Wadd (read Wadd or Wudd) nor Suwā‘, nor Yaghūth and Ya‘ūq and Nasr” — these being the names of their idols.

f:
وَقَدْ أَضَلُّوا كَثِيرًا ۖ وَلَا تَزِدِ الظَّالِمِينَ إِلَّا ضَلَالًا [71:24]
"They have already misled many; and grant Thou no increase to the wrong-doers but in straying (from their mark)." [71:24]
b: And they have certainly led astray, by these [gods], many, people, by commanding them to worship them. And do not [O God] increase the evildoers except in error!’ (wa-lā tazidi’l-zālimīna illā dalālan is a supplement to qad adallū, ‘they have certainly led astray’): He [Noah عليه السلام] invoked God against them when it was revealed to him that, ‘None of your people will believe except he who has already believed’ [Q. 11:36].

f:
مِمَّا خَطِيئَاتِهِمْ أُغْرِقُوا فَأُدْخِلُوا نَارًا فَلَمْ يَجِدُوا لَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْصَارًا [71:25]
Because of their sins they were drowned (in the flood), and were made to enter the Fire (of Punishment): and they found- in lieu of Allah- none to help them. [71:25]
b: Because of (mimmā: mā indicates a relative clause) their iniquities (khatāyāhum: a variant reading has khatī’ātihim) they were drowned, by the Flood, then made to enter the Fire, with which they were punished underwater after drowning. And they did not find for themselves besides, that is to say, other than, God any helpers, to protect them against the chastisement.

f:
وَقَالَ نُوحٌ رَبِّ لَا تَذَرْ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ دَيَّارًا [71:26]
And Noah عليه السلام, said: "O my Lord! Leave not of the Unbelievers, a single one on earth! [71:26]
b: And Noah عليه السلام said, ‘My Lord, do not leave from among the disbelievers a single dweller upon the earth (dayyār means ‘one who inhabits a dwelling [dār]’), in other words, not one.

f:
إِنَّكَ إِنْ تَذَرْهُمْ يُضِلُّوا عِبَادَكَ وَلَا يَلِدُوا إِلَّا فَاجِرًا كَفَّارًا [71:27]
"For, if Thou dost leave (any of) them, they will but mislead Thy devotees, and they will breed none but wicked ungrateful ones. [71:27]
b: Assuredly if You leave them, they will lead Your servants astray, and will beget only disbelieving profligates (fājir and kaffār derive [respectively] from yafjuru and yakfuru): he said this on account of the mentioned revelation that had been given to him.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ قُلْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ أَنَّهُ اسْتَمَعَ نَفَرٌ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَقَالُوا إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنًا عَجَبًا [72:1]
Say: It has been revealed to me that a company of Jinns listened (to the Qur´an). They said, ´We have really heard a wonderful Recital! [72:1]
b: Say, O Muhammad (s), to people: ‘It has been revealed to me, that is to say, I have been informed by way of revelation from God, exalted be He, that (annahu: the [suffixed] pronoun is that of the matter) a company of the jinn, the jinn of Nasībīn. This was at the time of the morning prayer at Batn Nakhla, a location between Mecca and Tā’if — these [jinn] being those mentioned in God’s saying, And when We sent a company of jinn your way…’ [Q. 46:29] — listened, to my recitation, then said, to their people upon returning to them: “We have indeed heard a marvellous Qur’ān, whose clarity, the richness of its meanings and other aspects one marvels at,

f:
يَهْدِي إِلَى الرُّشْدِ فَآمَنَّا بِهِ ۖ وَلَنْ نُشْرِكَ بِرَبِّنَا أَحَدًا [72:2]
´It gives guidance to the Right, and we have believed therein: we shall not join (in worship) any (gods) with our Lord. [72:2]
b: which guides to rectitude, to faith and propriety. Therefore we believe in it and we will never, after this day, associate anyone with our Lord.

f:
وَأَنَّهُ تَعَالَىٰ جَدُّ رَبِّنَا مَا اتَّخَذَ صَاحِبَةً وَلَا وَلَدًا [72:3]
´And Exalted is the Majesty of our Lord: He has taken neither a wife nor a son. [72:3]
b: And [we believe] that (annahu: the pronoun in this and in the next two instances is that of the matter) — exalted be the majesty of our Lord, transcendent is His majesty and magnificence above what is ascribed to Him — He has taken neither spouse nor son.

f:
وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ سَفِيهُنَا عَلَى اللَّهِ شَطَطًا [72:4]
´There were some foolish ones among us, who used to utter extravagant lies against Allah; [72:4]
b: And that the fool among us, the ignorant one among us, used to utter atrocious lies against God, extreme calumny by attributing to Him a spouse and a son.

f:
وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ تَقُولَ الْإِنْسُ وَالْجِنُّ عَلَى اللَّهِ كَذِبًا [72:5]
´But we do think that no man or spirit should say aught that untrue against Allah. [72:5]
b: And we thought that (an: softened, that is to say, annahu) humans and jinn would never utter a lie against God, by attributing such things to Him, until we discovered their mendacity thereby. God, exalted be He, says:

f:
وَأَنَّهُ كَانَ رِجَالٌ مِنَ الْإِنْسِ يَعُوذُونَ بِرِجَالٍ مِنَ الْجِنِّ فَزَادُوهُمْ رَهَقًا [72:6]
´True, there were persons among mankind who took shelter with persons among the Jinns, but they increased them in folly. [72:6]
b: And that certain individuals of mankind used to seek the protection of certain individuals of the jinn, when they stopped over in dangerous places during their journeys — whereat every man would say, ‘I seek the protection of the lord of this place against the evil of the insolent ones in it’ — so that they increased them, by their seeking their protection, in oppressiveness, such that they would say, ‘We are now lords of jinn and humans!’.

f:
وَأَنَّهُمْ ظَنُّوا كَمَا ظَنَنْتُمْ أَنْ لَنْ يَبْعَثَ اللَّهُ أَحَدًا [72:7]
´And they (came to) think as ye thought, that Allah would not raise up any one (to Judgment). [72:7]
b: And they, namely, the jinn, thought just as you, O humans, thought, that (an: softened in place of the hardened form, that is to say, annahu) God would never raise anyone, after his death.

f:
وَأَنَّا لَمَسْنَا السَّمَاءَ فَوَجَدْنَاهَا مُلِئَتْ حَرَسًا شَدِيدًا وَشُهُبًا [72:8]
´And we pried into the secrets of heaven; but we found it filled with stern guards and flaming fires. [72:8]
b: The jinn say: And we made for the heaven, we desired to listen by stealth, but we found it filled with mighty guards, from among the angels, and meteors, scorching stars: this was at the time of the sending of the Prophet ﷺ (s).

f:
وَأَنَّا كُنَّا نَقْعُدُ مِنْهَا مَقَاعِدَ لِلسَّمْعِ ۖ فَمَنْ يَسْتَمِعِ الْآنَ يَجِدْ لَهُ شِهَابًا رَصَدًا [72:9]
´We used, indeed, to sit there in (hidden) stations, to (steal) a hearing; but any who listen now will find a flaming fire watching him in ambush. [72:9]
b: And we used to, that is to say, before his Mission, sit in [certain] places therein to listen in; but anyone listening now will find a meteor lying in wait for him, aimed at him, ready to strike him.

f:
وَأَنَّا لَا نَدْرِي أَشَرٌّ أُرِيدَ بِمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ أَرَادَ بِهِمْ رَبُّهُمْ رَشَدًا [72:10]
´And we understand not whether ill is intended to those on earth, or whether their Lord (really) intends to guide them to right conduct. [72:10]
b: And we do not know, by not being able to eavesdrop by stealth, whether ill is intended for those who are in the earth, or whether their Lord intends for them good.

f:
وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الصَّالِحُونَ وَمِنَّا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ ۖ كُنَّا طَرَائِقَ قِدَدًا [72:11]
´There are among us some that are righteous, and some the contrary: we follow divergent paths. [72:11]
b: And that among us some have become righteous, after having listened to the Qur’ān, and some of us are otherwise, that is to say, a folk who are unrighteous; we are [made up of] different sects, opposing groups, [some] submitters to God and [others] disbelievers.

f:
وَأَنَّا ظَنَنَّا أَنْ لَنْ نُعْجِزَ اللَّهَ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَنْ نُعْجِزَهُ هَرَبًا [72:12]
´But we think that we can by no means frustrate Allah throughout the earth, nor can we frustrate Him by flight. [72:12]
b: And we assume that (an: softened in place of the hardened form, that is to say, annahu) we will never be able to elude God in the earth, nor will we be able to elude Him by fleeing — we will not be able to escape Him, whether we are on earth or, fleeing from it, in the heavens.

f:
وَأَنَّا لَمَّا سَمِعْنَا الْهُدَىٰ آمَنَّا بِهِ ۖ فَمَنْ يُؤْمِنْ بِرَبِّهِ فَلَا يَخَافُ بَخْسًا وَلَا رَهَقًا [72:13]
´And as for us, since we have listened to the Guidance, we have accepted it: and any who believes in his Lord has no fear, either of a short (account) or of any injustice. [72:13]
b: And that when we heard the guidance, the Qur’ān, we believed in it. For whoever believes in his Lord (read an implied huwa, ‘he’, [before fa-lā yakhāfu]) shall fear neither loss, a diminishing of his good deeds, nor oppression, [nor] injustice, by having his evil deeds increased.

f:
وَأَنَّا مِنَّا الْمُسْلِمُونَ وَمِنَّا الْقَاسِطُونَ ۖ فَمَنْ أَسْلَمَ فَأُولَٰئِكَ تَحَرَّوْا رَشَدًا [72:14]
´Amongst us are some that submit their wills (to Allah), and some that swerve from justice. Now those who submit their wills - they have sought out (the path) of right conduct: [72:14]
b: And that among us some have submitted [to God], while some of us are unjust, tyrants — on account of their disbelief. So whoever has submitted [to God], those are the ones who seek right guidance.

f:
وَأَمَّا الْقَاسِطُونَ فَكَانُوا لِجَهَنَّمَ حَطَبًا [72:15]
´But those who swerve,- they are (but) fuel for Hell-fire´- [72:15]
b: And as for those are unjust, they will be firewood, fuel, for Hell!” ’ (annā, annahum, and annahu totalling all twelve instances [above], including innahu ta‘ālā and annā minnā’l-muslimūna and what comes in between them may be read with a kasra [sc. innā, innahum etc.] indicating a new sentence [every time], or with a fatha [sc. annā, annahum etc.] indicating the statement that will follow [as a relative clause]).

f:
وَأَنْ لَوِ اسْتَقَامُوا عَلَى الطَّرِيقَةِ لَأَسْقَيْنَاهُمْ مَاءً غَدَقًا [72:16]
(And Allah´s Message is): "If they (the Pagans) had (only) remained on the (right) Way, We should certainly have bestowed on them Rain in abundance. [72:16]
b: God, exalted be He, says [the following] about the Meccan disbelievers: And [it has been revealed to me] that if they (allaw: softened in place of the hardened form, its subject having been omitted, that is to say, annahum [law], which is a supplement to annahu istama‘a, ‘that [a company of jinn] listened’) adopt the [right] path, the path of submission [to God], We will give them abundant water to drink, plenteous [water], from the heaven — this was after rain had been withheld from them for seven years —

f:
لِنَفْتِنَهُمْ فِيهِ ۚ وَمَنْ يُعْرِضْ عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّهِ يَسْلُكْهُ عَذَابًا صَعَدًا [72:17]
"That We might try them by that (means). But if any turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, He will cause him to undergo a severe Penalty. [72:17]
b: so that We may try them, test them, therein, and so know, through knowledge outwardly manifested, the nature of their gratitude. And whoever turns away from the remembrance of his Lord, [from] the Qur’ān, We will admit him (naslukhu, or read [first person] yaslukhu, ‘He will admit him’) into a tortuous chastisement.

f:
وَأَنَّ الْمَسَاجِدَ لِلَّهِ فَلَا تَدْعُوا مَعَ اللَّهِ أَحَدًا [72:18]
"And the places of worship are for Allah (alone): So invoke not any one along with Allah; [72:18]
b: And [it has been revealed to me] that the places of prayer belong to God, so do not invoke, in them, anyone along with God, by associating others with Him, like the Jews and Christians do, who, when they enter their churches and temples, they ascribe partners to God.

f:
وَأَنَّهُ لَمَّا قَامَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَدْعُوهُ كَادُوا يَكُونُونَ عَلَيْهِ لِبَدًا [72:19]
"Yet when the Devotee of Allah stands forth to invoke Him, they just make round him a dense crowd." [72:19]
b: And that (annahu; or innahu as a new sentence, the pronoun being that of the matter) when the servant of God, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (s), rose to invoke Him, to worship Him, at Batn Nakhla, they, that is, the jinn listening to his recitation, were almost upon him in heaps (libadan or lubadan, the plural of libda [or lubda], like felt in the way they were heaped on top of one another, crowding in their eagerness to listen to the Qur’ān).

f:
قُلْ إِنَّمَا أَدْعُو رَبِّي وَلَا أُشْرِكُ بِهِ أَحَدًا [72:20]
Say: "I do no more than invoke my Lord, and I join not with Him any (false god)." [72:20]
b: He said, in response to the disbelievers saying, ‘Abandon this affair of yours!’ (a variant reading [for qāla, ‘he said’], has qul, ‘Say:’) ‘I invoke only my Lord, as God, and I do not associate anyone with Him’.

f:
قُلْ إِنِّي لَا أَمْلِكُ لَكُمْ ضَرًّا وَلَا رَشَدًا [72:21]
Say: "It is not in my power to cause you harm, or to bring you to right conduct." [72:21]
b: Say: ‘I truly have no power to bring you any harm, to lead [you] astray, or any guidance’, any good.

f:
قُلْ إِنِّي لَنْ يُجِيرَنِي مِنَ اللَّهِ أَحَدٌ وَلَنْ أَجِدَ مِنْ دُونِهِ مُلْتَحَدًا [72:22]
Say: "No one can deliver me from Allah (If I were to disobey Him), nor should I find refuge except in Him, [72:22]
b: Say: ‘Indeed none shall protect me from God, from His chastisement, were I to disobey Him, and I shall never find besides Him, that is, other than Him, any refuge.

f:
إِلَّا بَلَاغًا مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرِسَالَاتِهِ ۚ وَمَنْ يَعْصِ اللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُ فَإِنَّ لَهُ نَارَ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا أَبَدًا [72:23]
"Unless I proclaim what I receive from Allah and His Messages: for any that disobey Allah and His Messenger,- for them is Hell: they shall dwell therein for ever." [72:23]
b: [I have power to bring you] only a communication (illā balāghan is excepted from the direct object clause of amliku, ‘I have power [to bring]’, that is to say, I have power only to communicate [the Message] to you, from God, that is, on His behalf, and His Messages (wa-risālātihi is a supplement to balāghan, ‘a communication’; what comes between the excepted clause and the clause from which it is excepted is a parenthetical statement intended to emphasise the preclusion of [the Prophet’s ﷺ] ‘ability [to bring them anything else]’). And whoever disobeys God and His Messenger, concerning the affirmation of [His] Oneness, and hence does not believe — indeed there will be for him the fire of Hell, abiding (khālidīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the person indicated by man, ‘whoever’, in lahu, ‘for him’, taking into account its [plural] import; it [khālidīna] is also an implied circumstantial qualifier, in other words, they shall enter it with their abiding having been preordained) therein forever’.

f:
حَتَّىٰ إِذَا رَأَوْا مَا يُوعَدُونَ فَسَيَعْلَمُونَ مَنْ أَضْعَفُ نَاصِرًا وَأَقَلُّ عَدَدًا [72:24]
At length, when they see (with their own eyes) that which they are promised,- then will they know who it is that is weakest in (his) helper and least important in point of numbers. [72:24]
b: Such that when they see (hattā is for inceptiveness, [but] also entailing a purposive sense to an implied preceding clause, that is to say, they persist in their disbelief until they come to see …) what they are promised, of chastisement, they will then know, at the moment that it befalls them, [either] on the day of Badr or on the Day of Resurrection, who is weaker in supporters and fewer in numbers, in assistants: is it them or the believers — according to the former [reading]? Or, is it Me or them, according to the latter. Some of them said, ‘When will this promise be [fulfilled]?’, whereupon the following was revealed:

f:
قُلْ إِنْ أَدْرِي أَقَرِيبٌ مَا تُوعَدُونَ أَمْ يَجْعَلُ لَهُ رَبِّي أَمَدًا [72:25]
Say: "I know not whether the (Punishment) which ye are promised is near, or whether my Lord will appoint for it a distant term. [72:25]
b: Say: ‘I do not know if what you are promised, of chastisement, is near, or if my Lord has set a [distant] length for it, an extent and a term which only He knows.

f:
عَالِمُ الْغَيْبِ فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِ أَحَدًا [72:26]
"He (alone) knows the Unseen, nor does He make any one acquainted with His Mysteries,- [72:26]
b: Knower [He is] of the Unseen, what is hidden from servants, and He does not disclose, He [does not] reveal, His Unseen to anyone, from mankind,

f:
إِلَّا مَنِ ارْتَضَىٰ مِنْ رَسُولٍ فَإِنَّهُ يَسْلُكُ مِنْ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِ رَصَدًا [72:27]
"Except a messenger whom He has chosen: and then He makes a band of watchers march before him and behind him, [72:27]
b: except to a messenger of whom He approves. Then, in addition to disclosing to him what He will [to disclose] of it, by way of [making it] a miracle for him, He despatches, He appoints and sends forth, before him, namely, the Messenger ﷺ, and behind him watchers, angels to preserve him until He has conveyed [it] to him as part of the [entire] revelation,

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُزَّمِّلُ [73:1]
O thou folded in garments! [73:1]
b: O you enwrapped in your garment!, the Prophet ﷺ (al-muzzammil is actually al-mutazammil, but the tā’ has been assimilated with the zāy), that is to say, the one who wraps himself up in his clothes when the Revelation [Gabriel عليه السلام] comes to him, in fear of him because of his awe-inspiring presence.

f:
قُمِ اللَّيْلَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا [73:2]
Stand (to prayer) by night, but not all night,- [73:2]
b: Stand vigil, perform prayer, through the night, except a little,

f:
نِصْفَهُ أَوِ انْقُصْ مِنْهُ قَلِيلًا [73:3]
Half of it,- or a little less, [73:3]
b: a half of it (nisfahu substitutes for qalīlan, with ‘little’ [being little by] taking into account the whole [night]), or reduce of it, of the half, a little, up to a third,

f:
أَوْ زِدْ عَلَيْهِ وَرَتِّلِ الْقُرْآنَ تَرْتِيلًا [73:4]
Or a little more; and recite the Qur´an in slow, measured rhythmic tones. [73:4]
b: or add to it, up to two thirds (aw implies [free] choice), and recite the Qur’ān, recite it carefully, in a measured tone.

f:
إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا [73:5]
Soon shall We send down to thee a weighty Message. [73:5]
b: Verily [soon] We shall cast on you a weighty, an awe-inspiring or stern, word, [a weighty] Qur’ān, because of the prescriptions [imposed] in it.

f:
إِنَّ نَاشِئَةَ اللَّيْلِ هِيَ أَشَدُّ وَطْئًا وَأَقْوَمُ قِيلًا [73:6]
Truly the rising by night is most potent for governing (the soul), and most suitable for (framing) the Word (of Prayer and Praise). [73:6]
b: Assuredly rising in the night, to wake up after [having been in] sleep, is firmer in tread, [more] conducive to [establishing] harmony between the hearing and the heart for the purpose of comprehending the Qur’ān, and more upright in respect to speech, clearer for utterance [of devotions].

f:
إِنَّ لَكَ فِي النَّهَارِ سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا [73:7]
True, there is for thee by day prolonged occupation with ordinary duties: [73:7]
b: [For] assuredly during the day you have extended engagements, administering your affairs, and you do not have the time to recite Qur’ān.

f:
وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ وَتَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا [73:8]
But keep in remembrance the name of thy Lord and devote thyself to Him whole-heartedly. [73:8]
b: And mention the Name of your Lord, that is, say, bi’smi’Llāhi’l-rahmāni’l-rahīm, ‘In the Name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful’, to begin your recitation, and devote yourself [exclusively] to Him with complete devotion (tabtīlan is the verbal noun from batala, used here [instead of tabattulan] in order to concord with the end-rhyme of the verses) for he [the Prophet ﷺ] is obliged to devote himself to God.

f:
رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَاتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا [73:9]
(He is) Lord of the East and the West: there is no god but He: take Him therefore for (thy) Disposer of Affairs. [73:9]
b: He is, Lord of the east and the west; there is no god except Him, so take Him for a Guardian, entrusting your affairs to Him,

f:
وَاصْبِرْ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاهْجُرْهُمْ هَجْرًا جَمِيلًا [73:10]
And have patience with what they say, and leave them with noble (dignity). [73:10]
b: and bear patiently what they say, that is, the disbelievers of Mecca, in the way of their maltreatment [of you], and part with them in a gracious manner, without any anguish — this was [revealed] before the command to fight them.

f:
وَذَرْنِي وَالْمُكَذِّبِينَ أُولِي النَّعْمَةِ وَمَهِّلْهُمْ قَلِيلًا [73:11]
And leave Me (alone to deal with) those in possession of the good things of life, who (yet) deny the Truth; and bear with them for a little while. [73:11]
b: And leave Me [to deal] with the deniers (wa’l-mukadhdhibīna is a supplement to the direct object, or [it is] an object of accompaniment; the meaning is: ‘I will avail you of them’, they being the doughty [leaders] of Quraysh), those enjoying affluence, and respite them a little, while — they were killed soon afterwards at Badr.

f:
إِنَّ لَدَيْنَا أَنْكَالًا وَجَحِيمًا [73:12]
With Us are Fetters (to bind them), and a Fire (to burn them), [73:12]
b: [For] indeed with Us are heavy fetters (ankāl is the plural of nikl), heavy shackles, and a hell-fire, a scorching Fire,

f:
وَطَعَامًا ذَا غُصَّةٍ وَعَذَابًا أَلِيمًا [73:13]
And a Food that chokes, and a Penalty Grievous. [73:13]
b: and a food that chokes, one that causes the throat to choke, and this is [either] zaqqūm [cf. Q. 44:43], darī‘ [cf. Q. 88:6], ghislīn [cf. Q. 69:36] or thorns of fire, which can neither be vomited nor ingested, and a painful chastisement, in addition to the [punishment] mentioned, for those who deny the Prophet ﷺ (s),

f:
يَوْمَ تَرْجُفُ الْأَرْضُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَكَانَتِ الْجِبَالُ كَثِيبًا مَهِيلًا [73:14]
One Day the earth and the mountains will be in violent commotion. And the mountains will be as a heap of sand poured out and flowing down. [73:14]
b: on the day when the earth and the mountains will quake and the mountains will be like heaps of shifting sand (mahīl derives from hāla, yahīlu; it is actually mahyūl, but the damma sound is considered too heavy for the yā’ and is therefore transposed onto the hā’, while the wāw, the second of two unvocalised consonants, is omitted on account of it being extra, and the damma is replaced by a kasra because of its [phonetic] affinity the [letter] yā’).

f:
إِنَّا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَيْكُمْ رَسُولًا شَاهِدًا عَلَيْكُمْ كَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا إِلَىٰ فِرْعَوْنَ رَسُولًا [73:15]
We have sent to you, (O men!) a messenger, to be a witness concerning you, even as We sent a messenger to Pharaoh. [73:15]
b: We have indeed sent to you, O people of Mecca, a Messenger, namely, Muhammad (s), to be a witness against you, on the Day of Resurrection to any disobedience that you engage in, just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger, namely, Moses, peace be upon him.

f:
فَعَصَىٰ فِرْعَوْنُ الرَّسُولَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُ أَخْذًا وَبِيلًا [73:16]
But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger; so We seized him with a heavy Punishment. [73:16]
b: But Pharaoh disobeyed the messenger, so We seized him with a severe seizing.

f:
فَكَيْفَ تَتَّقُونَ إِنْ كَفَرْتُمْ يَوْمًا يَجْعَلُ الْوِلْدَانَ شِيبًا [73:17]
Then how shall ye, if ye deny (Allah), guard yourselves against a Day that will make children hoary-headed?- [73:17]
b: So, if you disbelieve, in this world, how will you guard against a day (yawman is the direct object of tattaqūna, ‘you guard against’) that is, against the chastisement thereof, by what defence will you defend yourselves against the chastisement of a day, that will make the children grey-haired (shīb is the plural of ashyab) by the severity of its terrors, this being the Day of Resurrection (the shīn of shīb should actually have a damma, but it is given a kasra because of its [phonetic] affinity with the yā’) — a distressing day is described as being ‘a day that makes the forelocks of children turn grey’, which is [usually] understood figuratively; but it may be that in the case of this verse it is meant literally —

f:
السَّمَاءُ مُنْفَطِرٌ بِهِ ۚ كَانَ وَعْدُهُ مَفْعُولًا [73:18]
Whereon the sky will be cleft asunder? His Promise needs must be accomplished. [73:18]
b: with the heaven being rent asunder thereon, on that Day, because of its severity. His promise, exalted be He, of the coming of that [Day], shall be fulfilled, that is to say, it will come to pass without doubt.

f:
إِنَّ هَٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ ۖ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا [73:19]
Verily this is an Admonition: therefore, whoso will, let him take a (straight) path to his Lord! [73:19]
b: Indeed these, threatening verses, are a reminder, an admonition for all creatures. Let him who will, then, choose a way to his Lord, a path [to Him], through faith and obedience.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ يَا أَيُّهَا الْمُدَّثِّرُ [74:1]
O thou wrapped up (in the mantle)! [74:1]
b: O you enveloped in your mantle, the Prophet ﷺ (s) (al-muddaththir is actually al-mutadaththir, but the tā’ has been assimilated with the dāl) that is to say, the one who is enwrapped in his clothes when the Revelation [Gabriel عليه السلام] comes down on him,

f:
قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ [74:2]
Arise and deliver thy warning! [74:2]
b: arise and warn: threaten the people of Mecca with [punishment in] the Fire should they refuse to believe;

f:
وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ [74:3]
And thy Lord do thou magnify! [74:3]
b: and magnify your Lord, exalt [Him] above what is ascribed [to Him] by the idolaters;

f:
وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ [74:4]
And thy garments keep free from stain! [74:4]
b: and purify your clothes, from impurity, or [it means] shorten them, instead of [imitating] the way in which the Arabs [are wont to] let their robes drag [behind them], out of vanity, for perhaps they will be sullied by some impurity;

f:
وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ [74:5]
And all abomination shun! [74:5]
b: and shun [all] defilement, [this rijz] was explained by the Prophet ﷺ (s) to be the graven images; in other words, persist in shunning them.

f:
وَلَا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ [74:6]
Nor expect, in giving, any increase (for thyself)! [74:6]
b: And do not grant a favour seeking greater gain (read tastakthiru as a circumstantial qualifier) in other words, do not give something in order to demand more in return: this [stipulation] is specific to the Prophet ﷺ (s), since he is enjoined to [adopt] the fairest traits and the noblest of manners;

f:
وَلِرَبِّكَ فَاصْبِرْ [74:7]
But, for thy Lord´s (Cause), be patient and constant! [74:7]
b: and endure patiently for the sake of your Lord, [all His] commands and prohibitions.

f:
فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي النَّاقُورِ [74:8]
Finally, when the Trumpet is sounded, [74:8]
b: For when the trumpet is sounded, when the trumpet is blown, that is, the Horn (qarn), at the second blast,

f:
فَذَٰلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ [74:9]
That will be- that Day - a Day of Distress,- [74:9]
b: that day, that is to say, the time of the sounding (yawma’idhin is a substitution for the preceding subject, and is not declined because it is annexed to something that cannot be declined; the predicate of the subject [is the following]) will be a harsh day (idhā is operated by what is indicated by the statement: ishtadda’l-amru, ‘[for when the trumpet is sounded] the situation will be terrible’),

f:
عَلَى الْكَافِرِينَ غَيْرُ يَسِيرٍ [74:10]
Far from easy for those without Faith. [74:10]
b: for the disbelievers, not at all easy: herein is an indication that it will be easy for believers despite its harshness.

f:
ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيدًا [74:11]
Leave Me alone, (to deal) with the (creature) whom I created (bare and) alone!- [74:11]
b: Leave Me [to deal] with him whom I created (wa-man khalaqtu is a supplement to the direct object, or [it is] an object of accompaniment) lonely (wahīdan is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the man, ‘whom’, or to the pronoun referring to it but omitted from khalaqtu [sc. khalaqtuhu]), alone, without family or wealth — this was al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī —

f:
وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالًا مَمْدُودًا [74:12]
To whom I granted resources in abundance, [74:12]
b: and [then] assigned him ample means, abundant and continuous, [generated] from [his] crops, livestock and commerce,

f:
وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا [74:13]
And sons to be by his side!- [74:13]
b: and sons, ten or more, present [by his side], present at social gatherings and whose testimonies are listened to,

f:
وَمَهَّدْتُ لَهُ تَمْهِيدًا [74:14]
To whom I made (life) smooth and comfortable! [74:14]
b: and facilitated, extended, for him greatly, [his] livelihood, duration of life and children.

f:
ثُمَّ يَطْمَعُ أَنْ أَزِيدَ [74:15]
Yet is he greedy-that I should add (yet more);- [74:15]
b: Still he is eager that I should give [him] more.

f:
كَلَّا ۖ إِنَّهُ كَانَ لِآيَاتِنَا عَنِيدًا [74:16]
By no means! For to Our Signs he has been refractory! [74:16]
b: Nay!, I shall not give him more than that. He is indeed stubborn to Our signs, [to] the Qur’ān.

f:
سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا [74:17]
Soon will I visit him with a mount of calamities! [74:17]
b: [Soon] I shall burden him with a trying chastisement; alternatively [sa‘ūdan means] a mountain of fire which he will be made to ascend and then fall down from, forever.

f:
إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ [74:18]
For he thought and he plotted;- [74:18]
b: Indeed he pondered, what to say about the Qur’ān which he heard from the Prophet ﷺ (s), and decided, this, in his mind.

f:
فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ [74:19]
And woe to him! How he plotted!- [74:19]
b: Perish he, may he be cursed and chastised, how he decided!, [perish he] whatever the nature of his decision may have been.

f:
ثُمَّ قُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ [74:20]
Yea, Woe to him; How he plotted!- [74:20]
b: Again, perish he, how he decided!

f:
ثُمَّ نَظَرَ [74:21]
Then he looked round; [74:21]
b: Then he contemplated, the faces of his people; or [he contemplated] with what [words] he might cast aspersions upon it.

f:
ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ [74:22]
Then he frowned and he scowled; [74:22]
b: Then he frowned, he contracted his face and glowered, anguished by what he wanted to say, and scowled, increasing the contracting and the glowering [in his face].

f:
ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ [74:23]
Then he turned back and was haughty; [74:23]
b: Then he turned his back, to faith, in disdain, scornful of following the Prophet ﷺ (s),

f:
فَقَالَ إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ [74:24]
Then said he: "This is nothing but magic, derived from of old; [74:24]
b: and said, of what he [the Prophet ﷺ] had brought: ‘This is nothing but handed-down sorcery, learnt from sorcerers;

f:
إِنْ هَٰذَا إِلَّا قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ [74:25]
"This is nothing but the word of a mortal!" [74:25]
b: this is nothing but the speech of humans’, similar to what they [the idolaters] had said: ‘It is only a human that is teaching him’ [Q. 16:103].

f:
سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ [74:26]
Soon will I cast him into Hell-Fire! [74:26]
b: I shall [soon] admit him into Saqar! — Hell.

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا سَقَرُ [74:27]
And what will explain to thee what Hell-Fire is? [74:27]
b: And how would you know what is Saqar? — this [interrogative] is intended to emphasise its enormity.

f:
لَا تُبْقِي وَلَا تَذَرُ [74:28]
Naught doth it permit to endure, and naught doth it leave alone!- [74:28]
b: It neither spares nor leaves behind, anything of flesh or nerve, but destroys it [all], after which he is restored to his former state.

f:
لَوَّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ [74:29]
Darkening and changing the colour of man! [74:29]
b: It burns away the flesh, scorching the surface of skin.

f:
عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ [74:30]
Over it are Nineteen. [74:30]
b: There are nineteen [keepers] standing over it, angels, its keepers; a certain disbeliever, who was a mighty stalwart, said, ‘I will avail you seventeen of them, if you avail me [just] two’. God, exalted be He, says:

f:
وَمَا جَعَلْنَا أَصْحَابَ النَّارِ إِلَّا مَلَائِكَةً ۙ وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ إِلَّا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَيَزْدَادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِيمَانًا ۙ وَلَا يَرْتَابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۙ وَلِيَقُولَ الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْكَافِرُونَ مَاذَا أَرَادَ اللَّهُ بِهَٰذَا مَثَلًا ۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشَاءُ ۚ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ إِلَّا هُوَ ۚ وَمَا هِيَ إِلَّا ذِكْرَىٰ لِلْبَشَرِ [74:31]
And We have set none but angels as Guardians of the Fire; and We have fixed their number only as a trial for Unbelievers,- in order that the People of the Book may arrive at certainty, and the Believers may increase in Faith,- and that no doubts may be left for the People of the Book and the Believers, and that those in whose hearts is a disease and the Unbelievers may say, "What symbol doth Allah intend by this?" Thus doth Allah leave to stray whom He pleaseth, and guide whom He pleaseth: and none can know the forces of thy Lord, except He and this is no other than a warning to mankind. [74:31]
b: And We have appointed only angels as wardens of the Fire, in other words, and so they cannot be withstood as these [disbelievers are wont to] imagine; and We have made their number, so, only as a stumbling-block, a cause for error, for those who disbelieve, when they then say, ‘Why are there nineteen of them?’, so that those who were given the Scripture, namely, the Jews, may be certain, of the sincerity of the Prophet ﷺ (s) in [saying that] they are nineteen, for this concords with what is in their Scripture; and that those who believe, from among the People of the Scripture, may increase in faith, in affirmation of the truth, given that what the Prophet ﷺ (s) has said concords with what is in their Scripture, and that those given the Scripture and the believers, [those] other than these [Jews], may not be in doubt, concerning the number of [these] angels, and that those in whose hearts there is a sickness, an uncertainty, [those] in Medina, and the disbelievers, in Mecca, may say, ‘What did God mean by this, number [as a], similitude?’ (mathalan: they referred to it thus [as a mathal] on account of it being a curious matter; in terms of syntax, it [mathalan] is a circumstantial qualifier). Thus, that is, just as the one who rejects this number is led astray and the one who affirms the truth of it is guided, God leads astray whom He will and guides whom He will. And none knows the hosts of your Lord, namely, the angels, [none knows them] in terms of their strength and their assistants, except Him. And it, that is, Saqar, is nothing but a reminder for humans.

f:
كَلَّا وَالْقَمَرِ [74:32]
Nay, verily: By the Moon, [74:32]
b: Nay, (kallā: denoting a commencement [of a new sentence], to be understood as alā) by the moon!

f:
وَاللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ [74:33]
And by the Night as it retreateth, [74:33]
b: And by the night when it returns! (if read as idhā dabara), when it comes back after day (a variant reading has idh adbara, meaning ‘when it has receded’).

f:
وَالصُّبْحِ إِذَا أَسْفَرَ [74:34]
And by the Dawn as it shineth forth,- [74:34]
b: And by the dawn when it appears!

f:
إِنَّهَا لَإِحْدَى الْكُبَرِ [74:35]
This is but one of the mighty (portents), [74:35]
b: Verily it, that is, Saqar, is one of the enormities, [one of] the greatest calamities —

f:
نَذِيرًا لِلْبَشَرِ [74:36]
A warning to mankind,- [74:36]
b: a warning (nadhīran is a circumstantial qualifier referring to ihdā, ‘one of’, and it is masculine because it denotes [masculine] ‘adhāb, ‘chastisement’) to [all] humans;

f:
لِمَنْ شَاءَ مِنْكُمْ أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ أَوْ يَتَأَخَّرَ [74:37]
To any of you that chooses to press forward, or to follow behind;- [74:37]
b: [alike] to those of you who wish (li-man shā’a minkum is a substitution for li’l-bashar, ‘to [all] humans’) to advance, towards good, or towards Paradise by means of faith, or linger behind, in evil, or in Hell because of [their] disbelief.

f:
كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ [74:38]
Every soul will be (held) in pledge for its deeds. [74:38]
b: Every soul is held to ransom by what it earns, [it is] ransomed and requited for its deeds with the Fire,

f:
إِلَّا أَصْحَابَ الْيَمِينِ [74:39]
Except the Companions of the Right Hand. [74:39]
b: except those of the right [hand], namely, the believers who will be saved from it, and [who] will be,

f:
فِي جَنَّاتٍ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ [74:40]
(They will be) in Gardens (of Delight): they will question each other, [74:40]
b: in gardens, questioning one another,

f:
عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ [74:41]
And (ask) of the Sinners: [74:41]
b: about the guilty, and their predicament; and they will say to them, after all those who believed in the One God (muwahhidūn) are brought out of the Fire:

f:
مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ [74:42]
"What led you into Hell Fire?" [74:42]
b: ‘What has landed you in, [what has] made you enter, Saqar?’

f:
قَالُوا لَمْ نَكُ مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ [74:43]
They will say: "We were not of those who prayed; [74:43]
b: They will say, ‘We were not of those who prayed.

f:
وَلَمْ نَكُ نُطْعِمُ الْمِسْكِينَ [74:44]
"Nor were we of those who fed the indigent; [74:44]
b: Nor did we [ever] feed the needy.

f:
وَكُنَّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الْخَائِضِينَ [74:45]
"But we used to talk vanities with vain talkers; [74:45]
b: And we used to delve, into falsehood, along with those who delved,

f:
وَكُنَّا نُكَذِّبُ بِيَوْمِ الدِّينِ [74:46]
"And we used to deny the Day of Judgment, [74:46]
b: and we used to deny the Day of Judgement, [the Day] of Resurrection and Requital,

f:
حَتَّىٰ أَتَانَا الْيَقِينُ [74:47]
"Until there came to us (the Hour) that is certain." [74:47]
b: until [finally] the inevitable came to us’ — death.

f:
فَمَا تَنْفَعُهُمْ شَفَاعَةُ الشَّافِعِينَ [74:48]
Then will no intercession of (any) intercessors profit them. [74:48]
b: Thus the intercession of the intercessors, from among the angels, the prophets and the righteous, will not avail them, in other words, there will be no intercession for them.

f:
فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ [74:49]
Then what is the matter with them that they turn away from admonition?- [74:49]
b: So what (fa-mā: the subject) is wrong with them (lahum: the predicate thereof, semantically connected to an omitted clause, the person of which has been transposed onto it) that they turn away (mu‘ridīna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the [suffixed] pronoun [in lahum, ‘them’]) from the Reminder — in other words, ‘what has happened to them that they have turned away from admonition’ —

f:
كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ [74:50]
As if they were affrighted asses, [74:50]
b: as if they were wild asses

f:
فَرَّتْ مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ [74:51]
Fleeing from a lion! [74:51]
b: fleeing from a lion?, that is to say, fleeing from it with absolute fright.

f:
بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنْهُمْ أَنْ يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفًا مُنَشَّرَةً [74:52]
Forsooth, each one of them wants to be given scrolls (of revelation) spread out! [74:52]
b: Nay, but everyone of them desires to be given unrolled scrolls, from God, exalted be He, [enjoining them] to follow the Prophet ﷺ (s), as they said [before], ‘And [even then] we will not believe your ascension until you bring down for us a book that we may read’ [Q. 17:93].

f:
كَلَّا ۖ بَلْ لَا يَخَافُونَ الْآخِرَةَ [74:53]
By no means! But they fear not the Hereafter, [74:53]
b: No indeed! (kallā: a deterrent of what they desire). Rather they do not fear the Hereafter, that is, the chastisement thereof.

f:
كَلَّا إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ [74:54]
Nay, this surely is an admonition: [74:54]
b: No indeed! (kallā: a commencement [of a new sentence]) Assuredly it, that is, the Qur’ān, is a Reminder, an admonition.

f:
فَمَنْ شَاءَ ذَكَرَهُ [74:55]
Let any who will, keep it in remembrance! [74:55]
b: So whoever wills shall remember it, he shall read it and be admonished by it.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ [75:1]
I do call to witness the Resurrection Day; [75:1]
b: Nay! (the lā is extra in both instances) I swear by the Day of Resurrection.

f:
وَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ [75:2]
And I do call to witness the self-reproaching spirit: (Eschew Evil). [75:2]
b: And, nay, I swear by the (self-)reproaching soul, the one that reproaches itself, even if it should expend great effort in being virtuous (the response to the oath has been omitted, that is to say, la-tub‘athunna, ‘you shall indeed be resurrected!’, as indicated by [what follows]):

f:
أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَلَّنْ نَجْمَعَ عِظَامَهُ [75:3]
Does man think that We cannot assemble his bones? [75:3]
b: Does man, that is, [does] the disbeliever, suppose that We shall not assemble his bones?, for the raising [from the graves] and [for] the bringing back to life.

f:
بَلَىٰ قَادِرِينَ عَلَىٰ أَنْ نُسَوِّيَ بَنَانَهُ [75:4]
Nay, We are able to put together in perfect order the very tips of his fingers. [75:4]
b: Yes, indeed!, We shall assemble them. We are able, in addition to assembling them, to reshape [even] his fingers, that is to say, to restore their bones just as they had been, despite their smallness: so how much more so [are We able to restore] the larger ones!

f:
بَلْ يُرِيدُ الْإِنْسَانُ لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ [75:5]
But man wishes to do wrong (even) in the time in front of him. [75:5]
b: Nay, but man desires to deny (li-yafjura: the lām is extra, and the subjunctive mood is because of an implied [preceding] an, ‘that’) what lies ahead of him, namely, the Day of Resurrection, as is indicated by:

f:
يَسْأَلُ أَيَّانَ يَوْمُ الْقِيَامَةِ [75:6]
He questions: "When is the Day of Resurrection?" [75:6]
b: He asks, ‘When is the Day of Resurrection?’ — the question is meant in mockery and denial.

f:
فَإِذَا بَرِقَ الْبَصَرُ [75:7]
At length, when the sight is dazed, [75:7]
b: But when the eyes are dazzled (read bariqa or baraqa), startled and perplexed upon seeing some of those things which it used to deny;

f:
وَخَسَفَ الْقَمَرُ [75:8]
And the moon is buried in darkness. [75:8]
b: and the moon is eclipsed, darkening, its light disappearing,

f:
وَجُمِعَ الشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ [75:9]
And the sun and moon are joined together,- [75:9]
b: and the sun and the moon are brought together, so that both of them will rise from the west; or [it means when] the light of both of them disappears — and this will be on the Day of Resurrection —

f:
يَقُولُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ [75:10]
That Day will Man say: "Where is the refuge?" [75:10]
b: on that day man will say, ‘Where is the escape?’

f:
كَلَّا لَا وَزَرَ [75:11]
By no means! No place of safety! [75:11]
b: No indeed! — a deterrent against seeking to escape — There is no refuge, no shelter to seek protection in.

f:
إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمُسْتَقَرُّ [75:12]
Before thy Lord (alone), that Day will be the place of rest. [75:12]
b: On that day the recourse will be to your Lord, the [final] recourse of all creatures, whereupon they will be reckoned with and requited.

f:
يُنَبَّأُ الْإِنْسَانُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بِمَا قَدَّمَ وَأَخَّرَ [75:13]
That Day will Man be told (all) that he put forward, and all that he put back. [75:13]
b: On that day man will be informed of what he has sent ahead and left behind, [he will be informed] of the his first and last deeds.

f:
بَلِ الْإِنْسَانُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ بَصِيرَةٌ [75:14]
Nay, man will be evidence against himself, [75:14]
b: Rather man has insight into his [own] soul, for his limbs will speak of his deeds (the hā’ [sc. the tā’ marbūta in basīratun] is for hyperbole), and so he must be requited,

f:
وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُ [75:15]
Even though he were to put up his excuses. [75:15]
b: though he should offer his excuses (ma‘ādhīr is the plural of ma‘dhira, but following a different pattern [from the usual ma‘dhira, ma‘ādhir]) that is to say, whatever excuse he offers will not be accepted from him.

f:
لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسَانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ [75:16]
Move not thy tongue concerning the (Qur´an) to make haste therewith. [75:16]
b: God, exalted be He, says to His Prophet: Do not move your tongue with it, with the Qur’ān, before Gabriel عليه السلام is through with [reciting] it, to hasten it, fearing to lose it.

f:
إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ [75:17]
It is for Us to collect it and to promulgate it: [75:17]
b: Assuredly it is for Us to bring it together, in your breast, and to recite it, your reciting of it, that is, its flowing off your tongue.

f:
فَإِذَا قَرَأْنَاهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ [75:18]
But when We have promulgated it, follow thou its recital (as promulgated): [75:18]
b: So, when We recite it, to you, by means of Gabriel’s عليه السلام recital, follow its recitation, listen to its recitation: thus the Prophet ﷺ (s) would listen to it and then repeat it.

f:
ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ [75:19]
Nay more, it is for Us to explain it (and make it clear): [75:19]
b: Then, it is for Us to explain it, by making you comprehend [it]: the connection between this verse and what preceded [it] is that those [verses before] imply turning away from God’s signs, whereas this one implies applying oneself to them by memorising them.

f:
كَلَّا بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ [75:20]
Nay, (ye men!) but ye love the fleeting life, [75:20]
b: No indeed! (kallā is for commencement, with the sense of alā) Rather you love the transitory [life], this world (both verbs [here and below] may be read in the second or third person plural),

f:
وَتَذَرُونَ الْآخِرَةَ [75:21]
And leave alone the Hereafter. [75:21]
b: and forsake the Hereafter, thus neglecting to work towards [attaining bliss in] it.

f:
وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ نَاضِرَةٌ [75:22]
Some faces, that Day, will beam (in brightness and beauty);- [75:22]
b: Some faces on that day, that is, on the Day of Resurrection, will be radiant, fair and resplendent,

f:
إِلَىٰ رَبِّهَا نَاظِرَةٌ [75:23]
Looking towards their Lord; [75:23]
b: looking upon their Lord, in other words, they will see God, glorified and exalted be He, in the Hereafter.

f:
وَوُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَاسِرَةٌ [75:24]
And some faces, that Day, will be sad and dismal, [75:24]
b: And other faces on that day will be scowling, glowering, frowning terribly,

f:
تَظُنُّ أَنْ يُفْعَلَ بِهَا فَاقِرَةٌ [75:25]
In the thought that some back-breaking calamity was about to be inflicted on them; [75:25]
b: certain that a spine-crushing calamity will fall on them, a great catastrophe, one that ‘crushes the spine’ (fiqār).

f:
كَلَّا إِذَا بَلَغَتِ التَّرَاقِيَ [75:26]
Yea, when (the soul) reaches to the collar-bone (in its exit), [75:26]
b: No indeed! (kallā: in the sense of alā) When it, the soul, reaches up to the collar bones,

f:
وَقِيلَ مَنْ ۜ رَاقٍ [75:27]
And there will be a cry, "Who is a magician (to restore him)?" [75:27]
b: and it is said, [and] those around him [the dying one] say: ‘Where is the enchanter?’, to perform incantations on him and cure him,

f:
وَظَنَّ أَنَّهُ الْفِرَاقُ [75:28]
And he will conclude that it was (the Time) of Parting; [75:28]
b: and he suspects, [he] the one whose soul has reached this [stage], that it is the [time of] parting, the parting with this world,

f:
وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ [75:29]
And one leg will be joined with another: [75:29]
b: and the shank is intertwined with the [other] shank, that is, one of his shanks [will be intertwined] with his other shank at the moment of death; or [it means] the distress of parting with this world is intertwined with the distress of the arrival of the Hereafter;

f:
إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْمَسَاقُ [75:30]
That Day the Drive will be (all) to thy Lord! [75:30]
b: on that day to your Lord will be the driving [of the souls] (al-masāq means al-sawq; this indicates the operator of the [above] idhā, ‘when’, the meaning being: ‘when the soul reaches the throat, it will be driven towards the judgement of its Lord’).

f:
فَلَا صَدَّقَ وَلَا صَلَّىٰ [75:31]
So he gave nothing in charity, nor did he pray!- [75:31]
b: For he, man, neither affirmed [the truth] nor prayed,

f:
وَلَٰكِنْ كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ [75:32]
But on the contrary, he rejected Truth and turned away! [75:32]
b: but he denied, the Qur’ān, and he turned away, from faith,

f:
ثُمَّ ذَهَبَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِ يَتَمَطَّىٰ [75:33]
Then did he stalk to his family in full conceit! [75:33]
b: then went off to his family swaggering, strutting about in self-conceit.

f:
أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ [75:34]
Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe! [75:34]
b: [Woe be] nearer to you (there is a shift from the third [to the second] person address here; the term [awlā] is a noun of action, with the [following] lām being explicative, in other words, ‘what you are averse to is [now] near to you’) and nearer, that is because you are more deserving of it [woe] than anyone else,

f:
ثُمَّ أَوْلَىٰ لَكَ فَأَوْلَىٰ [75:35]
Again, Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe! [75:35]
b: then [may woe be] nearer to you and nearer! — [repeated] for emphasis.

f:
أَيَحْسَبُ الْإِنْسَانُ أَنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى [75:36]
Does man think that he will be left uncontrolled, (without purpose)? [75:36]
b: Does man suppose that he is to be left aimless?, left to his own devices without being obligated to the [prescribed] laws: let him not suppose that!

f:
أَلَمْ يَكُ نُطْفَةً مِنْ مَنِيٍّ يُمْنَىٰ [75:37]
Was he not a drop of sperm emitted (in lowly form)? [75:37]
b: Was he not — that is, [indeed] he was — a drop of emitted semen? (read yumnā or tumnā) deposited into the womb.

f:
ثُمَّ كَانَ عَلَقَةً فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ [75:38]
Then did he become a leech-like clot; then did (Allah) make and fashion (him) in due proportion. [75:38]
b: Then it, the drop of semen, became a clot; then He, God, created, from it man, and proportioned [him], making the parts of his body upright,

f:
فَجَعَلَ مِنْهُ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَىٰ [75:39]
And of him He made two sexes, male and female. [75:39]
b: and made of it, of the drop of semen that became a blood-clot, then an embryo, a [small] mass of flesh, the two sexes, the two kinds, the male and the female, at times coming together and at times each being on their own.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ هَلْ أَتَىٰ عَلَى الْإِنْسَانِ حِينٌ مِنَ الدَّهْرِ لَمْ يَكُنْ شَيْئًا مَذْكُورًا [76:1]
Has there not been over Man a long period of Time, when he was nothing - (not even) mentioned? [76:1]
b: Has there [ever] been — there has indeed [been] — for man, Adam عليه السلام, a period of time, forty years, in which he was a thing unmentioned? — he was during this [period] a fashioned in clay and not mentioned; alternatively what is meant by insān, ‘man’, is the generic noun and by hīn, ‘a period of time’, the period of gestation.

f:
إِنَّا خَلَقْنَا الْإِنْسَانَ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ أَمْشَاجٍ نَبْتَلِيهِ فَجَعَلْنَاهُ سَمِيعًا بَصِيرًا [76:2]
Verily We created Man from a drop of mingled sperm, in order to try him: So We gave him (the gifts), of Hearing and Sight. [76:2]
b: Verily We created man, the species, from a drop of mixed fluid, [from] a mixture, that is from the [seminal] fluid of the man and the [ovarian] fluid of the woman that have mixed and blended, so that We may test him, trying him with the moral obligations [of religion] (nabtalīhi is either a new sentence [‘We will test him’], or an implied circumstantial qualifier, meaning ‘intending to test him when he is ready’). So We made him, for that [very] reason, hearing, seeing.

f:
إِنَّا هَدَيْنَاهُ السَّبِيلَ إِمَّا شَاكِرًا وَإِمَّا كَفُورًا [76:3]
We showed him the Way: whether he be grateful or ungrateful (rests on his will). [76:3]
b: Verily We have guided him to the way, We have pointed out to him the path of guidance by sending messengers [to mankind], whether he be grateful, that is to say, [whether he be] a believer, or ungrateful (both [shākiran and kafūran] are circumstantial qualifiers referring to the direct object; in other words, We have pointed out to him in both presupposed states, whether his gratefulness or his unthankfulness; immā is used to list the ‘states’).

f:
إِنَّا أَعْتَدْنَا لِلْكَافِرِينَ سَلَاسِلَ وَأَغْلَالًا وَسَعِيرًا [76:4]
For the Rejecters we have prepared chains, yokes, and a blazing Fire. [76:4]
b: We have assuredly prepared for the disbelievers chains, with which they are dragged through the Fire, and fetters, around their necks to which the chains will be attached, and a hell-fire, a fire set ablaze, burning fiercely, in which they shall be chastised.

f:
إِنَّ الْأَبْرَارَ يَشْرَبُونَ مِنْ كَأْسٍ كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا كَافُورًا [76:5]
As to the Righteous, they shall drink of a Cup (of Wine) mixed with Kafur,- [76:5]
b: Truly the righteous (abrār is the plural of barr or bārr), namely, the obedient ones, will drink from a cup (ka’s is a vessel for drinking wine and this [wine] will be in it; what is meant is [that they will drink] from ‘wine’, [a case where] the actuality is referred to by the name of the locus [in which it is found]; min, ‘from, is partitive) whose mixture, that with which it is mixed, is camphor;

f:
عَيْنًا يَشْرَبُ بِهَا عِبَادُ اللَّهِ يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا [76:6]
A Fountain where the Devotees of Allah do drink, making it flow in unstinted abundance. [76:6]
b: a spring (‘aynan substitutes for kāfūran), containing the scent thereof, from which the servants of God, His friends, drink, making it gush forth plenteously, directing it to wherever they wish of their dwellings.

f:
يُوفُونَ بِالنَّذْرِ وَيَخَافُونَ يَوْمًا كَانَ شَرُّهُ مُسْتَطِيرًا [76:7]
They perform (their) vows, and they fear a Day whose evil flies far and wide. [76:7]
b: They fulfil their vows, [pledged] in obedience to God, and fear a day the evil of which will be widespread.

f:
وَيُطْعِمُونَ الطَّعَامَ عَلَىٰ حُبِّهِ مِسْكِينًا وَيَتِيمًا وَأَسِيرًا [76:8]
And they feed, for the love of Allah, the indigent, the orphan, and the captive,- [76:8]
b: And they give food, despite [their] love of it, that is to say, [despite their love] of food and their craving for it, to the needy, the poor, and the orphan, who does not have a father, and the prisoner, meaning the one who has been rightly imprisoned.

f:
إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ اللَّهِ لَا نُرِيدُ مِنْكُمْ جَزَاءً وَلَا شُكُورًا [76:9]
(Saying),"We feed you for the sake of Allah alone: no reward do we desire from you, nor thanks. [76:9]
b: ‘We feed you only for the sake of God, seeking His reward. We do not desire any reward from you, nor any thanks: this contains the reason for the giving of the food. Now, do they actually say this, or is it that God knows this [to be true] of them and has thus praised them by [mentioning] it? The two are different opinions [regarding this matter].

f:
إِنَّا نَخَافُ مِنْ رَبِّنَا يَوْمًا عَبُوسًا قَمْطَرِيرًا [76:10]
"We only fear a Day of distressful Wrath from the side of our Lord." [76:10]
b: Indeed we fear from our Lord a day of frowning, one in which faces scowl, in other words, a horrid day to observe on account of its severity, calamitous’, severe in that respect.

f:
فَوَقَاهُمُ اللَّهُ شَرَّ ذَٰلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا [76:11]
But Allah will deliver them from the evil of that Day, and will shed over them a Light of Beauty and (blissful) Joy. [76:11]
b: God has therefore shielded them from the evil of that day, and has granted them radiance, fairness and resplendence in their faces, and joy.

f:
وَجَزَاهُمْ بِمَا صَبَرُوا جَنَّةً وَحَرِيرًا [76:12]
And because they were patient and constant, He will reward them with a Garden and (garments of) silk. [76:12]
b: And He has rewarded them for their patience, for their steadfastness in refraining from disobedience, with a Garden, into which they are admitted, and silk, which they are given to wear;

f:
مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا عَلَى الْأَرَائِكِ ۖ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِيهَا شَمْسًا وَلَا زَمْهَرِيرًا [76:13]
Reclining in the (Garden) on raised thrones, they will see there neither the sun´s (excessive heat) nor (the moon´s) excessive cold. [76:13]
b: reclining (muttaki’īna is a circumstantial qualifier referring to the subject of the implicit [verb] udkhilūhā, ‘they are admitted into it’) therein upon couches (arā’ik are beds inside canopies). They will not find (lā yarawna is a second circumstantial qualifier) therein either sun or bitter cold, neither heat nor cold; but it is also said that zamharīr means ‘the moon’, and so, in other words, it [means that it] will be bright without any sun or moon.

f:
وَدَانِيَةً عَلَيْهِمْ ظِلَالُهَا وَذُلِّلَتْ قُطُوفُهَا تَذْلِيلًا [76:14]
And the shades of the (Garden) will come low over them, and the bunches (of fruit), there, will hang low in humility. [76:14]
b: And close (dāniyatan is a supplement to the [syntactical] locus of the clause lā yarawna, in other words, [it is a supplement to the import] ghayra rā’īna) over them will be its shades, its trees, and its clusters [of fruits] will hang low, its fruits will brought close, so that they are reached by the one standing, the one sitting or the one lying down.

f:
وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِآنِيَةٍ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَأَكْوَابٍ كَانَتْ قَوَارِيرَا [76:15]
And amongst them will be passed round vessels of silver and goblets of crystal,- [76:15]
b: And they will be waited upon from all around them, in it, with vessels of silver, and goblets (akwāb are cups without handles) of crystal —

f:
قَوَارِيرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا [76:16]
Crystal-clear, made of silver: they will determine the measure thereof (according to their wishes). [76:16]
b: crystal of silver, that is, they are made of silver which is transparent like crystal — which they, that is, the ones passing around them [in service], have measured in a precise measure, according to the measure required by the one drinking it, neither more nor less, which makes for a most delightful drink.

f:
وَيُسْقَوْنَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا كَانَ مِزَاجُهَا زَنْجَبِيلًا [76:17]
And they will be given to drink there of a Cup (of Wine) mixed with Zanjabil,- [76:17]
b: And they will be given to drink therein a cup, wine, whose mixture, that with which it is mixed, is ginger,

f:
عَيْنًا فِيهَا تُسَمَّىٰ سَلْسَبِيلًا [76:18]
A fountain there, called Salsabil. [76:18]
b: a spring (‘aynan substitutes for zanjabīlan, ‘ginger’) therein named Salsabīl, meaning that its water is like ginger, which the Arabs find very tasteful, [and which is] very palatable for the throat.

f:
وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ وِلْدَانٌ مُخَلَّدُونَ إِذَا رَأَيْتَهُمْ حَسِبْتَهُمْ لُؤْلُؤًا مَنْثُورًا [76:19]
And round about them will (serve) youths of perpetual (freshness): If thou seest them, thou wouldst think them scattered Pearls. [76:19]
b: And they will be waited upon by immortal youths, [immortally] in the form of youths, never ageing, whom, when you see them you will suppose them, because of their beauty and the way in which they are scattered about [offering] service, to be scattered pearls, [strewn] from their string, or from their shells, in which they are fairer than [when they, the pearls, are] otherwise [not in their shells].

f:
وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ثَمَّ رَأَيْتَ نَعِيمًا وَمُلْكًا كَبِيرًا [76:20]
And when thou lookest, it is there thou wilt see a Bliss and a Realm Magnificent. [76:20]
b: And when you look there, that is to say, when you begin to look about in Paradise, you will see (ra’ayta is the response to idhā, ‘when’) bliss, that is indescribable, and a great kingdom, vast, without limit.

f:
عَالِيَهُمْ ثِيَابُ سُنْدُسٍ خُضْرٌ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٌ ۖ وَحُلُّوا أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ فِضَّةٍ وَسَقَاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَرَابًا طَهُورًا [76:21]
Upon them will be green Garments of fine silk and heavy brocade, and they will be adorned with Bracelets of silver; and their Lord will give to them to drink of a Wine Pure and Holy. [76:21]
b: Upon them (‘āliyahum is in the accusative as an adverbial clause, and constitutes the predicate of a subject that will follow; a variant reading has ‘ālīhim as a subject, with what follows as its predicate; the suffixed pronoun [-hum] denotes those persons to whom the supplement refers) will be garments of fine green silk and [heavy] silk brocade (sundus is fine silk and constitutes the outer cushion, while istabraq is coarse silk and constitutes the inner lining; either read thiyābu sundusin khudrun wa’stabraqin or thiyābu sundusin khudrin wa’stabraqun, or thiyābu sundusin khudrun wa’stabraqun, or wa-thiyābu sundusin khudrin wa’stabraqin). And they will be adorned with bracelets of silver — elsewhere it is stated, ‘of gold’, in order to show that they will be adorned with both types at the same time or separately — and their Lord will give them a pure drink to drink (tahūran, ‘pure’, is intended as a hyperbolic qualification of its purity and cleanness, in contrast to the wine of this world).

f:
إِنَّ هَٰذَا كَانَ لَكُمْ جَزَاءً وَكَانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُورًا [76:22]
"Verily this is a Reward for you, and your Endeavour is accepted and recognised." [76:22]
b: ‘Verily this, bliss, is a reward for you, and your endeavour has been appreciated’.

f:
إِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ الْقُرْآنَ تَنْزِيلًا [76:23]
It is We Who have sent down the Qur´an to thee by stages. [76:23]
b: Assuredly We (nahnu reiterates the subject of innā, ‘assuredly, for the purpose of emphasis; alternatively it is a separating pronoun) have revealed the Qur’ān to you as a gradual revelation (tanzīlan is the predicate of inna, ‘assuredly’), in other words, We have divided it into parts instead of not revealing it all at once.

f:
فَاصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِمًا أَوْ كَفُورًا [76:24]
Therefore be patient with constancy to the Command of thy Lord, and hearken not to the sinner or the ingrate among them. [76:24]
b: So submit patiently to your Lord’s decree, to you to deliver His Message, and do not obey of them, that is, [of] the disbelievers, any sinner or disbeliever, namely, ‘Utba b. Rabī‘a and al-Walīd b. al-Mughīra — both of whom said to the Prophet ﷺ (s), ‘Abandon this affair of yours!’; it is also possible that what is meant is every sinner or disbeliever, in other words, ‘Do not obey any of these, whichever of the two he may be, in what he may summon you to of sin or disbelief’.

f:
وَاذْكُرِ اسْمَ رَبِّكَ بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا [76:25]
And celebrate the name of thy Lord morning and evening, [76:25]
b: And mention the Name of your Lord, during prayer, at dawn and with the declining of the sun, that is, at dawn (fajr), noon (zuhr) and in the afternoon (‘asr);

f:
وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَاسْجُدْ لَهُ وَسَبِّحْهُ لَيْلًا طَوِيلًا [76:26]
And part of the night, prostrate thyself to Him; and glorify Him a long night through. [76:26]
b: and prostrate to Him for a portion of the night, that is, at after sunset (maghrib) and at night (‘ishā’), and glorify Him the length of the night: perform supererogatory prayers during it, as mentioned above, for either two thirds, a half or a third of it.

f:
إِنَّ هَٰؤُلَاءِ يُحِبُّونَ الْعَاجِلَةَ وَيَذَرُونَ وَرَاءَهُمْ يَوْمًا ثَقِيلًا [76:27]
As to these, they love the fleeting life, and put away behind them a Day (that will be) hard. [76:27]
b: Assuredly these love the transitory [life], this world, and leave behind them a burdensome day, an awful [one], namely, the Day of Resurrection, not working towards it.

f:
نَحْنُ خَلَقْنَاهُمْ وَشَدَدْنَا أَسْرَهُمْ ۖ وَإِذَا شِئْنَا بَدَّلْنَا أَمْثَالَهُمْ تَبْدِيلًا [76:28]
It is We Who created them, and We have made their joints strong; but, when We will, We can substitute the like of them by a complete change. [76:28]
b: We created them and made firm their frames, their limbs and their joints, and, whenever We will, We can completely replace them with others like them, in terms of their created form, in place of them, by destroying them (tabdīlan, ‘completely’, is for emphasis; idhā, ‘when’, functions in the sense of in, ‘if’, similar to [where God says in several places], in yasha’ yudhhibkum, If He will, He can take you away [cf. Q. 14:19]; but because He, exalted be He, has not willed this, it has not happened thus far).

f:
إِنَّ هَٰذِهِ تَذْكِرَةٌ ۖ فَمَنْ شَاءَ اتَّخَذَ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِ سَبِيلًا [76:29]
This is an admonition: Whosoever will, let him take a (straight) Path to his Lord. [76:29]
b: This, sūra, is indeed a reminder, an admonition for [all] creatures. Let him who will, then, choose a way to his Lord, a path, through obedience.

f:
وَمَا تَشَاءُونَ إِلَّا أَنْ يَشَاءَ اللَّهُ ۚ إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًا [76:30]
But ye will not, except as Allah wills; for Allah is full of Knowledge and Wisdom. [76:30]
b: But you will not (tashā’ūna, may also be read yashā’ūna, ‘they will’), choose a way through obedience, unless God wills, this. Assuredly God is ever Knower, of His creatures, Wise, in what He does.

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ وَالْمُرْسَلَاتِ عُرْفًا [77:1]
By the (Winds) sent forth one after another (to man´s profit); [77:1]
b: By those sent in succession (‘urfan), that is, [by] the winds that follow [one another] in succession, like the mane (‘urf) of a horse, one part [of hair] coming after the other (‘urfan is in the accusative because it is a circumstantial qualifier);

f:
فَالْعَاصِفَاتِ عَصْفًا [77:2]
Which then blow violently in tempestuous Gusts, [77:2]
b: by the raging hurricanes, the violent winds;

f:
وَالنَّاشِرَاتِ نَشْرًا [77:3]
And scatter (things) far and wide; [77:3]
b: by the sweeping spreaders, [by] the winds that scatter the rains;

f:
فَالْفَارِقَاتِ فَرْقًا [77:4]
Then separate them, one from another, [77:4]
b: by the decisive discriminators, that is, [by] the verses of the Qur’ān, which discriminate between truth and falsehood, and between what is lawful and what is unlawful;

f:
فَالْمُلْقِيَاتِ ذِكْرًا [77:5]
Then spread abroad a Message, [77:5]
b: by the casters of the remembrance, that is, [by] angels that descend with the revelation upon the prophets and messengers, casting the revelation onto the [various] communities [of mankind],

f:
عُذْرًا أَوْ نُذْرًا [77:6]
Whether of Justification or of Warning;- [77:6]
b: to excuse or to warn, that is to say, in order to excuse or to warn on behalf of God, exalted be He (a variant reading [for nudhran and ‘udhran] has nudhuran and ‘udhuran).

f:
إِنَّمَا تُوعَدُونَ لَوَاقِعٌ [77:7]
Assuredly, what ye are promised must come to pass. [77:7]
b: Surely that which you are promised, O disbelievers of Mecca, in the way of resurrection and chastisement, will befall: it will be, without any doubt.

f:
فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ [77:8]
Then when the stars become dim; [77:8]
b: So when the stars are obliterated, [when] their light is extinguished,

f:
وَإِذَا السَّمَاءُ فُرِجَتْ [77:9]
When the heaven is cleft asunder; [77:9]
b: and when the heaven is rent asunder,

f:
وَإِذَا الْجِبَالُ نُسِفَتْ [77:10]
When the mountains are scattered (to the winds) as dust; [77:10]
b: and when the mountains are blown away, crushed to pieces and blown in the air,

f:
وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ [77:11]
And when the messengers are (all) appointed a time (to collect);- [77:11]
b: and when the time is set for the [testimony of the] messengers (read uqqitat or wuqqitat), that is to say, [when] they are gathered to an appointed time,

f:
لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ [77:12]
For what Day are these (portents) deferred? [77:12]
b: For what day — for a tremendous day — has it been appointed?, [it has been appointed] for witnessing [of the messengers] against their communities [to the effect] that they delivered [their messages from God].

f:
لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ [77:13]
For the Day of Sorting out. [77:13]
b: For the Day of Decision, for creatures (from this one may infer the response to [the clauses beginning with] idhā, ‘when’, in other words, ‘[when …], the decision will be made for [all] creatures’).

f:
وَمَا أَدْرَاكَ مَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ [77:14]
And what will explain to thee what is the Day of Sorting out? [77:14]
b: And how would you know what the Day of Decision is? — emphasising the enormity of its terror.

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:15]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:15]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day! — a threat of chastisement for them.

f:
أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ [77:16]
Did We not destroy the men of old (for their evil)? [77:16]
b: Did We not destroy the ancients, for their denial, in other words, We certainly destroyed them,

f:
ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ [77:17]
So shall We make later (generations) follow them. [77:17]
b: then made the latter folk follow them?, [the latter folk] of those who denied, such as the disbelievers of Mecca, whom We will destroy.

f:
كَذَٰلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ [77:18]
Thus do We deal with men of sin. [77:18]
b: So, just as We dealt with those who denied, will We deal with the guilty, with every individual who will be guilty in the future, and destroy them.

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:19]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:19]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day! — [reiterated] for emphasis.

f:
أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ مِنْ مَاءٍ مَهِينٍ [77:20]
Have We not created you from a fluid (held) despicable?- [77:20]
b: Did We not create you from a base fluid, one that is delicate — and this is semen,

f:
فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ [77:21]
The which We placed in a place of rest, firmly fixed, [77:21]
b: then lodged it in a secure abode, that is, the womb,

f:
إِلَىٰ قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ [77:22]
For a period (of gestation), determined (according to need)? [77:22]
b: for a known span?, namely, the time for delivery.

f:
فَقَدَرْنَا فَنِعْمَ الْقَادِرُونَ [77:23]
For We do determine (according to need); for We are the best to determine (things). [77:23]
b: Thus We were able, to do this; so [how] excellent able ones We are!

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:24]
Ah woe, that Day! to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:24]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفَاتًا [77:25]
Have We not made the earth (as a place) to draw together. [77:25]
b: Have We not made the earth a receptacle (kifātan is a verbal noun, from kafata, meaning damma, ‘enclosed’), that is, an enclosure,

f:
أَحْيَاءً وَأَمْوَاتًا [77:26]
The living and the dead, [77:26]
b: for the living, on its surface, and the dead, inside it,

f:
وَجَعَلْنَا فِيهَا رَوَاسِيَ شَامِخَاتٍ وَأَسْقَيْنَاكُمْ مَاءً فُرَاتًا [77:27]
And made therein mountains standing firm, lofty (in stature); and provided for you water sweet (and wholesome)? [77:27]
b: and set therein soaring mountains and give you sweet water to drink?

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:28]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:28]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
انْطَلِقُوا إِلَىٰ مَا كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ [77:29]
(It will be said:) "Depart ye to that which ye used to reject as false! [77:29]
b: And on the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the deniers: Depart to that, chastisement, which you used to deny!

f:
انْطَلِقُوا إِلَىٰ ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلَاثِ شُعَبٍ [77:30]
"Depart ye to a Shadow (of smoke ascending) in three columns, [77:30]
b: Depart to a triple-forked shadow — this is the smoke of Hell, which, as it rises, splits into three parts because of its magnitude —

f:
لَا ظَلِيلٍ وَلَا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ [77:31]
"(Which yields) no shade of coolness, and is of no use against the fierce Blaze. [77:31]
b: which is neither shady, [neither] protective, [unable] to shade them from the heat of that Day, nor of any avail against, [nor] wards off from them anything of, the flame, the Fire.

f:
إِنَّهَا تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ [77:32]
"Indeed it throws about sparks (huge) as Forts, [77:32]
b: Indeed it, that is, the Fire, throws up sparks, namely, those [flame] that are thrown by it into the air, [huge] like palace edifices, in terms of their enormity and vertical extension,

f:
كَأَنَّهُ جِمَالَتٌ صُفْرٌ [77:33]
"As if there were (a string of) yellow camels (marching swiftly)." [77:33]
b: as if they were [dark] yellow camels (jimālātun is the plural of jimalatun, the plural of jamalun; a variant reading has jimālatun), in terms of their shape and colour. In hadīth [it is stated], ‘The sparks of humans [thrown into the air by the Fire] are black as pitch (qīr)’; the Arabs call dark camels sufr, ‘yellow’, because a touch of yellow is mixed with their blackish colour, and therefore it is said that ‘yellow’ in this verse [actually] means ‘black’, on account of what has been mentioned; but some say no [to this interpretation]; (sharar is the plural of sharāra; qīr is qār, ‘pitch’).

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:34]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:34]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
هَٰذَا يَوْمُ لَا يَنْطِقُونَ [77:35]
That will be a Day when they shall not be able to speak. [77:35]
b: This, namely, the Day of Resurrection, is the day in which they will not utter, anything,

f:
وَلَا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ [77:36]
Nor will it be open to them to put forth pleas. [77:36]
b: nor will they be given permission, to offer excuses, and so offer excuses (fa-ya‘tadhirūna is a supplement to yu’dhanu, ‘given permission’, but without being a direct result of it, since it belongs within the confines of the [general] denial [of permission], in other words, ‘there will be no permission, hence no excuses’).

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:37]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:37]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
هَٰذَا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ ۖ جَمَعْنَاكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ [77:38]
That will be a Day of Sorting out! We shall gather you together and those before (you)! [77:38]
b: ‘This is the Day of Decision. We have brought you, O deniers from this community, and the ancients together, [the ancients] from among the deniers before you, so that you will [all] be reckoned with and chastised together;

f:
فَإِنْ كَانَ لَكُمْ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ [77:39]
Now, if ye have a trick (or plot), use it against Me! [77:39]
b: So if you have any stratagems, any ploy to ward off your chastisement, try your strategems against Me!’ — put them into effect!

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:40]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:40]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلَالٍ وَعُيُونٍ [77:41]
As to the Righteous, they shall be amidst (cool) shades and springs (of water). [77:41]
b: Truly the God-fearing will be amid shades, that is, amid clusters of trees, since there is no sun therein from whose heat to seek shade, and springs, issuing forth with water,

f:
وَفَوَاكِهَ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ [77:42]
And (they shall have) fruits,- all they desire. [77:42]
b: and fruits such as they desire: this is meant to point out that eating and drinking in Paradise is [done] according to their desires, in contrast to [the case in] this world, where it is predominantly determined by what people are able to procure. It will also be said to them:

f:
كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئًا بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ [77:43]
"Eat ye and drink ye to your heart´s content: for that ye worked (Righteousness). [77:43]
b: ‘Eat and drink in [full] enjoyment (hanī’an is a circumstantial qualifier, in other words, mutahanni’īna) for what you used to do’, in the way of obedience.

f:
إِنَّا كَذَٰلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ [77:44]
Thus do We certainly reward the Doers of Good. [77:44]
b: Indeed so, in the same way that We reward the God-fearing, do We reward the virtuous.

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:45]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:45]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُجْرِمُونَ [77:46]
(O ye unjust!) Eat ye and enjoy yourselves (but) a little while, for that ye are Sinners. [77:46]
b: ‘Eat and enjoy — addressing the disbelievers in this world — for a little, time, at the end of which comes death — this is meant as a threat for them. Indeed you are guilty!’

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:47]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:47]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ارْكَعُوا لَا يَرْكَعُونَ [77:48]
And when it is said to them, "Prostrate yourselves!" they do not so. [77:48]
b: For when it is said to them, ‘Bow down!’, perform prayer, they do not bow down, they do not perform prayer.

f:
وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ [77:49]
Ah woe, that Day, to the Rejecters of Truth! [77:49]
b: Woe to the deniers on that day!

f:
بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ عَمَّ يَتَسَاءَلُونَ [78:1]
Concerning what are they disputing? [78:1]
b: About what, about what thing, are they, the people of Quraysh, questioning one another?

f:
عَنِ النَّبَإِ الْعَظِيمِ [78:2]
Concerning the Great News, [78:2]
b: About the awesome tiding ([this is] the explication of that ‘thing’; the interrogative is meant to emphasise its magnitude) — this [awesome tiding] is the Qur’ān, comprising [news of] the Resurrection and so on, which the Prophet ﷺ (s) brought —

f:
الَّذِي هُمْ فِيهِ مُخْتَلِفُونَ [78:3]
About which they cannot agree. [78:3]
b: concerning which they are at variance, for the believers affirm it, while the disbelievers repudiate it.

f:
كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ [78:4]
Verily, they shall soon (come to) know! [78:4]
b: No indeed! — a disavowal — they will come to know, what will befall them for their rejection of it.

f:
ثُمَّ كَلَّا سَيَعْلَمُونَ [78:5]
Verily, verily they shall soon (come to) know! [78:5]
b: Again, no indeed! They will come to know! ([reiterated] for emphasis; thumma is added here to declare that the second threat of chastisement is more severe than the first). God, exalted be He, then alludes to His power to resurrect, saying:

f:
أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ مِهَادًا [78:6]
Have We not made the earth as a wide expanse, [78:6]
b: Have We not made the earth a cradle, a bed, like a cradle,

f:
وَالْجِبَالَ أَوْتَادًا [78:7]
And the mountains as pegs? [78:7]
b: and the mountains pegs?, with which the earth is tied down like tents are tied down with pegs (the interrogative is meant as an affirmative).

f:
